Title: RENN Asia Wellness offers free health checks worth RM500,000
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A wellness centre is offering free health screenings worth RM500,000 to the first 1,000 Malaysians until Nov 30, or while the allocation lasts.
As part of the government's Hari Kebangsaan Hari Malaysia campaign,
RENN Asia Wellness
said the health checks comprise the AtCor Arterial Stiffness Test, Quantum Vitamin & Mineral Analysis and MicroCirculation Analysis.
The initiative aims to promote early detection and greater awareness of health risks, particularly cardiovascular diseases and other non-communicable diseases (NCDs).
RENN Asia Wellness founder and chief executive officer Jonathan Chew said preventive health should become part of routine health management rather than something considered only when a person feels unwell.
"Many health conditions can develop without obvious symptoms, which means not feeling unwell does not necessarily mean that everything is fine.
"Regular assessment gives people an opportunity to understand their health better and, where necessary, take appropriate action earlier," he said.
[[nid:1532731]]
The AtCor test evaluates central blood pressure and arterial stiffness, while the Quantum Vitamin & Mineral Analysis assesses vitamin and mineral status and the MicroCirculation Analysis examines blood circulation through the body's smallest blood vessels.
"Malaysia continues to face the long-term health and economic consequences of NCDs.
"Preventive health should therefore be viewed as a longer-term investment, rather than simply an additional healthcare expense," Chew added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PDZ Holdings proposes RM65.4mil capital reduction
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: PDZ Holdings Bhd (PDZ) has proposed a capital reduction exercise to cancel RM65.4 million of its issued share capital to set off against the company's accumulated losses.
In an announcement outlining the proposal, the company stated that the exercise will rationalise its financial standing to better reflect the value of its underlying assets and overall financial position.
This move is expected to enhance the group's credibility with bankers, suppliers, customers, and investors regarding its long-term operational sustainability and viability, said PDZ's principle adviser Sierac Corporate Advisers Sdn Bhd.
As of August 17, PDZ's issued share capital stands at RM158.57 million, comprising 588.37 million ordinary shares. Following the capital reduction, the issued share capital will be reduced to RM93.17 million, while maintaining the exact same total number of shares in issue.
Based on the group's unaudited 18-month financial statements as at June 30, 2026, the exercise will reduce its accumulated losses of RM65.46 million to RM176,000.
Meanwhile, at the group level, the accumulated losses of RM56.18 million will be transformed into positive retained earnings of RM9.1 million after accounting for the RM65.4 million credit and the estimated expenses.
The proposed capital reduction remains subject to shareholder approval at an extraordinary general meeting to be convened. The exercise is slated for completion in the first quarter of 2027, barring any unforeseen circumstances.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Petronas secured 5-year LNG supply agreement to Greece
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Petroliam Nasional Bhd's (Petronas) unit Petco Trading (UK) Ltd, has secured a five-year agreement to supply liquefied natural gas (LNG) to Greece, strengthening its presence in Europe and the wider Southeast European energy market.
Under the sale and purchase agreement with Greece's Metlen Energy and Metals Plc, Petco Trading will deliver six LNG cargoes annually from Petronas' Atlantic portfolio, equivalent to about 0.6 billion cubic metres per annum (bcma), starting in 2027.
In a statement, the national oil and gas company said the agreement marks another step in its strategy to expand its LNG presence across West of Suez markets, particularly Europe and the Mediterranean, while leveraging its global LNG portfolio and trading capabilities.
Petronas executive vice-president and chief executive officer of Gas & Maritime Business Datuk Adif Zulkifli said the agreement demonstrated the company's commitment to providing reliable and flexible LNG solutions as markets navigate energy security, affordability and energy transition priorities.
"This agreement with Metlen underscores Petronas' commitment to delivering reliable and flexible LNG solutions that support our customers' evolving energy needs.
"As markets continue to navigate energy security, affordability and transition priorities, Petronas remains focused on creating value through our global LNG portfolio, trading capabilities and trusted partnerships," he said.
Petronas, through Petco Trading, is also seeking to strengthen customer relationships in key growth markets as demand for diversified and reliable LNG supplies increases.
For Metlen, the agreement supports its strategy to diversify LNG sources and enhance flexibility and resilience in procurement.
This also contributes to security of supply in Greece and the wider Southeast European region.
At the same time, it reinforces Greece's position as a strategic regional energy hub.
Metlen chief executive director of international energy supply and trading Panayotis Kanellopoulos said the deal strengthened the company's LNG sourcing.
"By expanding our international synergies, as with this leading global LNG player, we further enhance flexibility and reliability of supply, supporting both our customers and the broader regional market, as well as Greece's energy hub credentials," he said.
The agreement also lays the foundation for further collaboration between Petronas and Metlen as both companies seek to support LNG supply diversification and energy resilience in Greece and Southeast Europe.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nepal tragedy: Families question search for 55 Malaysians
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Families of 55 Malaysians still unaccounted for after the Nepal disaster are questioning the timing and strategy of the search, 20 days after the tragedy.
Families in Hope spokesman Dr R. Manivannan, who represents 49 of the 55 affected families, said their concern was not about the dedication, professionalism or courage of SMART personnel, but the timing, strategy, prioritisation and what was actually achieved.
"Our concern is about timing, strategy, prioritisation and what was actually achieved," he said in a statement today.
The disaster occurred on Aug 26 along the Nepal-Tibet border, leaving 55 Malaysians unaccounted for.
Manivannan said SMART departed Malaysia on Sept 5, Day 11, while its first publicly reported movement into the affected operational area was on Sept 8, Day 14, when the team arrived in Dhunche and established a tactical forward operating base.
"We recognise that operational constraints existed. But after 20 days,
families are entitled to ask difficult questions,
" he said.
He said families had provided photographs, videos, timestamps, communications, travel movements, GPS-related evidence, eyewitness information, travel-group movements and immigration and checkpoint information.
Manivannan said three specific areas contained a significant proportion of the families' last-known-location information but, based on operational information released publicly, those areas did not appear to have been searched by SMART.
He said the families were not seeking to take over the operation, but wanted their information to be properly incorporated into the operational picture.
The families had requested that one or two representatives be given appropriate access to the National Security Council coordination mechanism to share information and allow it to be reconciled with information held by the government, he said.
The families were also seeking greater clarity on search, recovery and identification efforts on the Tibet side, including information on three Malaysians whom they said they were informed had crossed Tibetan immigration around Day 9.
Manivannan said they wanted details on who the three Malaysians were, when they crossed, their last confirmed locations and whether immigration, vehicle, passenger and CCTV records had been reviewed.
He also called for an objective review of the first 48 to 72 hours after the disaster, including whether all reasonable avenues for assistance had been pursued urgently.
The families had also sought a meeting with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, saying direct engagement was important to address their concerns and clarify what would happen next.
Manivannan said the families were now facing additional legal and financial issues involving loans, insurance, employment, property and other matters because of the prolonged uncertainty.
They wanted a coordinated government mechanism to assist them with these issues, he said.
The families were also seeking a clear operational plan following SMART's return, a
detailed briefing on areas searched
and what was found, continued engagement with Nepal and China, and a clear account of the forensic and identification process.
They also called for a communication protocol ensuring significant developments affecting the missing Malaysians were communicated promptly to next of kin.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Negri Sembilan DKU declares April proclamation invalid
Article:
SEREMBAN: The Negri Sembilan Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU) has declared that the proclamation dated April 19, 2026, relating to the abdication of Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir is unconstitutional and invalid.
Secretary Raja Norazli Raja Nordin said three of the four individuals who signed the proclamation did not hold the position of Undang under the adat of their respective luak on the date in question.
"Furthermore, Article 10(1) of the Negri Sembilan Laws of the Constitution 1959 stipulates that the Undang may only call upon His Royal Highness to abdicate or relinquish the position of Yang di-Pertuan Besar after a full and complete inquiry has been conducted.
"That condition is mandatory, yet no such inquiry was ever conducted, none was ever brought before the Dewan, and His Royal Highness was never given notice or the opportunity to be heard.
"Therefore, the proclamation dated April 19, 2026, was flawed from the outset," he said in a statement here following decisions reached at a special DKU meeting held in Seri Menanti, Kuala Pilah, yesterday.
Raja Norazli said that on April 20, the menteri besar holding office at the time refused to sign the proclamation under Article 10(2) of the Negri Sembilan Laws of the Constitution 1959, on the grounds that the conditions of Article 10 had not been met and that one of the signatories was not an Undang.
"With that refusal, the function of the Menteri Besar under Article 10(2) of the Negri Sembilan Laws of the Constitution 1959 had already been exercised, and the proclamation thereby lapsed and became void," he said.
He added that even though the new Menteri Besar subsequently signed the same proclamation — allegedly on Aug 3 — that act did not restore anything.
He said the new Menteri Besar could not re-execute a function that had already been exercised.
"If that were permitted, every change of Menteri Besar would revive the same proclamation and the matter would never end," he said.
On the media statement issued by the Undang on Sept 5 and the press conference held by the group three days later on Sept 8, Raja Norazli said those actions had no legal effect, as they relied entirely on the flawed and lapsed April 19 proclamation and the instrument dated Aug 3, which added nothing to its validity.
He said the position of Tuanku Muhriz as Yang di-Pertuan Besar remained intact, as no lawful process had ever caused His Royal Highness to cease holding that position.
"The Dewan does not recognise any vacancy and does not recognise any other person as holding that position.
"There can be no successor as long as the position is lawfully held. A person who does not hold a position cannot exercise the powers of that position," he said.
Raja Norazli said anything done in the name of a position that is not held has no effect under adat.
He said the position of Undang Luak Sungei Ujong is currently held by Dato' Klana Petra Muhammad Faris Johari; Undang Luak Rembau by Dato' Sedia Raja Hassan Ab Hamid; and Undang Luak Johol by Dato' Johan Pahlawan Lela Perkasa Setiawan Datuk Muhammed Abdullah.
The positions of Undang Luak Jelebu and Dato' Shahbandar Sungei Ujong remain vacant.
He said the actions of six individuals in signing the document dated Sept 5, 2026, were considered treasonous under adat and the law.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Four Chinese citizens to be charged over Kedah kidnapping
Article:
ALOR SETAR: Three men and a woman, all Chinese citizens, will be charged at the Alor Setar court tomorrow in connection with the kidnapping of a woman at a house in Taman Amira, Jalan Langgar, last month.
The four, aged between 24 and 46, are expected to face charges under Section 365 of the Penal Code.
On Aug 8, it was reported that
two foreign suspects were killed in a shootout
with police during a raid to rescue a kidnapping victim at a house in Taman Amira, Jalan Langgar.
Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk M. Kumar had said the incident occurred at about 8.40pm when a team from the Bukit Aman CID Special Investigation Division (D9) raided the residential area.
Following the incident, police conducted several raids at separate locations in Kedah, Penang and Kuala Lumpur.
Six people were arrested, comprising a local man, four foreign men and a foreign woman, aged in their 20s to 40s.
On Sept 10, one of the suspects was charged at the Alor Setar Sessions Court with kidnapping a woman from China last month.
The man pleaded not guilty to the charge.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesia's president sacks finance minister, promotes deputy
Article:
JAKARTA: Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto has sacked finance minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa and appointed his deputy Suahasil Nazara as his replacement, the president's office said on Monday.
Suahasil Nazara, deputy finance minister since 2019, was among senior officials who arrived at the state palace for a swearing-in ceremony, while Purbaya, 61, was earlier seen leaving during a parliamentary hearing.
"The priority is to run a credible state budget," Suahasil said after his inauguration, adding that he would commit to maintaining the fiscal deficit below the legislated limit of 3 per cent of GDP.
"I will continue to run a trustworthy state budget, ensure trustworthy public communication, and also ensure that what the state budget does supports the government's priority programmes."
Purbaya's sacking came just days after he marked one year in office, with Southeast Asia's largest economy suffering a crisis of confidence among investors and analysts.
The straight-talking Purbaya had replaced long-standing finance minister Sri Mulyani Indrawati in September last year as Prabowo sought aggressive pro-growth policies over fiscal prudence. He did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Purbaya's time in office was marked by a number of economic shocks, including a plummeting rupiah and a ballooning fiscal deficit. His policy of injecting quick liquidity into banks to spur growth also created friction with the central bank.
Two ratings agencies downgraded Indonesia's credit rating outlook from positive to negative this year, citing policy uncertainty and fiscal spending plans, battering sentiment on the US$1.4 trillion G20 economy.
The latest controversy surrounding Purbaya was his sudden announcement that sovereign wealth fund Danantara Indonesia would transfer 120 trillion rupiah (US$6.8 billion) of its profits to the government to help meet this year's fiscal deficit target. The head of Danantara later said no such plan had been discussed.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pacific Partnership 2026 shows strength of multinational cooperation, says US Admiral
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Differences in language, culture, and organisational structures did not prevent countries from working effectively together during Pacific Partnership 2026 (PP26), said US Pacific Fleet commander Admiral Stephen Thomas Koehler.
He said the two-week Malaysia leg demonstrated how nations could overcome those differences while working towards a common mission of strengthening disaster preparedness and response.
"We made the extremely difficult look easy, which is the demonstration of our professionalism. We did that with many different countries working together towards one mission.
"What we accomplished here proves that in the Pacific, the ocean is not what separates us — it's what brings us together," he said during the Malaysia Pacific Partnership closing ceremony at INTAN Sabah today.
[[nid:1532705]]
Koehler added that partnerships developed through the initiative reflected the broader US approach to the region, where relationships with allies and partners form an important component of regional strength.
He said the success of PP26 reflected a shared commitment among military and civilian organisations to strengthen disaster response capabilities.
"That success belongs to all of you – and it signifies our shared commitment to the Pacific Partnership mission: to promote cooperation between military and civilian organisations to prepare for disaster response," he said.
The Pacific Partnership was established following the 2004 Boxing Day tsunami, when the US military took part in the international relief effort.
PP26 involved nearly 1,500 personnel from Australia, Canada, Germany, Japan, South Korea, New Zealand, Singapore, the United Kingdom, the United States, and host nations.
The Malaysia leg, marking the country's
sixth Pacific Partnership
mission, focused on four main areas: disaster management, engineering, medical and public health, and community outreach.
Activities included
maritime
search-and-rescue diver training, disaster preparedness engagements, infrastructure improvements at Babagon Toki Primary School and Telipok Health Clinic, medical exchanges, interfaith dialogues, and educational programmes.
Meanwhile,
PP26 mission commander US Navy
Captain Robert Reyes said the mission will make its final stop in the Philippines, with about 250 personnel expected to arrive on Sept 16.
The opening ceremony is scheduled for Sept 18, while the mission will conclude on Sept 28 with a closing ceremony at Leyte Gulf Landing, where US Army General Douglas MacArthur came ashore in 1944.
Reyes said the Philippines leg would involve a footprint similar to Malaysia's, with additional specialised personnel brought in at the request of the host nation.
Malaysian armed forces Joint Forces Commander Lieutenant General Datuk Sri Tengku Muhammad Fauzi Tengku Ibrahim said PP26 provided an opportunity for Malaysia to work alongside government agencies, non-governmental organisations, and local communities.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Federal Court reserves decision on PKR's RM10 mil bond appeal against Zuraida
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Federal Court today reserved its decision on PKR's appeal to reinstate a High Court ruling ordering former Ampang member of parliament Datuk Zuraida Kamaruddin to pay RM10 million for breaching a party bond.
PKR counsel Ranjit Singh submitted that Zuraida had contractually admitted that the value conferred upon her exceeded RM10 million, while the bond's operative clause fixed that exact sum upon default.
"Zuraida admitted that the value conferred upon her exceeded RM10 million, while the operative clause fixed RM10 million as the sum payable upon the occurrence of the stipulated events," Ranjit said during the appeal against a Court of Appeal decision that reduced the quantum to RM100,000.
Ranjit submitted that the appeal ultimately turned on the legal consequence of a contractual admission of value where Section 75 of the Contracts Act is invoked.
"The recital recorded Zuraida's admission that the value conferred upon her exceeded RM10 million. Section 75 remains the statutory control against penal, oppressive or unconscionable stipulations. But it must be applied to the contract as it stands, including the facts contractually admitted by the parties," he said.
He added that while the bond was contractual in nature, it had been executed against the backdrop of the country's political landscape when party-hopping threatened government stability.
"One must read the bond in a manner that explains why the sum of RM10 million was stipulated, which at first glance may appear excessive. But the reality is, look at what happened. The Sheraton Move led to the collapse of the Pakatan Harapan coalition at the Federal level," Ranjit said, assisted by lawyer Navpreet Singh.
In response, Zuraida's counsel Tan Sri Azhar Azizan Harun contended that political agreements enjoyed no special exemption from Section 75 of the Contracts Act.
"The party cannot use its status and position as a political party to bypass statutory protections against penalty clauses. Section 75 of the Act does not cease to apply merely because the contractual obligations arose in the context of a political party.
"To hold otherwise would create, by judicial implication, an exception to Section 75. This court should not countenance such an approach," said Azhar, assisted by counsel Nizamuddin Hamid.
Azhar further argued that individual candidates lacked equal bargaining power when agreeing to unilateral candidate bonds.
"This unequal bargaining power is not dependent on the candidate's seniority or position in the party. The bond demonstrates that it was not an individually negotiated agreement in which the respondent freely negotiated and agreed that RM10 million represented a reasonable measure of compensation in the event of default.
"It was imposed on the respondent by the party," he said, adding that the RM100,000 sum set by the Court of Appeal was reasonable.
Following submissions, the three-member bench chaired by Chief Justice Tun Wan Ahmad Farid Wan Salleh, alongside Chief Judge of Sabah and Sarawak Datuk Azizah Nawawi and Federal Court Judge Datuk Azmi Ariffin, reserved its ruling to a date to be fixed later.
On June 24, 2025, the Federal Court granted PKR leave to appeal the matter.
The Court of Appeal had on Dec 11, 2024, upheld the High Court's finding that Zuraida breached the bond, but slashed the quantum from RM10 million to RM100,000.
On June 23, 2023, Kuala Lumpur High Court judge Datuk Akhtar Tahir had ruled in favour of PKR, declaring the bond valid and binding.
The lawsuit was filed in 2020 by PKR secretary-general Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail on behalf of the party after Zuraida left PKR following the 14th General Election in 2018.
Under the bond terms, Zuraida was required to pay PKR RM10 million within seven days if she resigned, joined another party, or became an independent after winning on a PKR ticket.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysian woman nabbed with 8kg of cannabis at Hong Kong airport
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A 33-year-old Malaysian woman was arrested in Hong Kong after she was allegedly caught attempting to smuggle about eight kilogrammes (kg) of cannabis buds worth HK$1.6 million (RM830,000) into the territory on Saturday.
Hong Kong Customs said the woman had arrived at Hong Kong International Airport from Bangkok, Thailand, before she was detained during a customs inspection.
"During the inspection, customs officers found about eight kg of suspected cannabis in her checked-in baggage.
"The woman was arrested, and investigations are ongoing," it said in a statement yesterday.
Hong Kong Customs said it would continue to step up enforcement against drug trafficking through intelligence-led analysis.
It also reminded the public not to become involved in drug trafficking for financial gain or accept offers from others to carry controlled items into or out of Hong Kong.
Under Hong Kong's Dangerous Drugs Ordinance, anyone convicted of trafficking in dangerous drugs can be fined up to HK$5 million (RM2.6 million) and sentenced to life imprisonment.
On July 30, a 27-year-old Malaysian man was arrested after about 3kg of cannabis worth HK$600,000 (RM311,000) was found in his checked-in baggage following his arrival from Bangkok.
Earlier, on July 16, a 19-year-old Malaysian man who arrived from Bangkok via Manila was also arrested after about 11kg of cannabis worth HK$2 million (RM1.04 million) was found in his checked-in baggage.
Another case involving a Malaysian national was recorded on July 9, when a 19-year-old man was arrested after arriving from Kuala Lumpur via Singapore with about 3kg of cannabis worth HK$500,000 (RM260,000) in his baggage.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Rohingya family living rough outside Bandar Baru Uda offices for a week
Article:
JOHOR BARU: A Rohingya family, including a pregnant woman and an infant, has been living rough on a pavement outside office buildings in Bandar Baru Uda here for about a week.
The family, comprising the woman and her children, has been sleeping on a carpet spread along the walkway at Jalan Padi 1.
Business operators in the area said the family's presence had caused inconvenience to people visiting nearby offices.
A company administrator working in the vicinity said several of the children, mostly boys, were frequently shirtless and made noise while playing along the pavement.
"They also often approach our office entrance, peering inside while pressing their faces against the glass door.
"We have informed the Welfare Department and hope the authorities will take appropriate action soon," she said.
The family's presence also went viral today after a post in the Pasal Johor Facebook group drew public attention to them.
A netizen, Omar Amat, called on the Johor Immigration Department to take action.
The development comes less than a month after the New Straits Times reported on Aug 24 that
another Rohingya family
had been living rough at various public places around Larkin.
That family had moved between a children's playground, shoplot areas and a location near a surau for more than two months whenever authorities were about to take action.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Negri Sembilan MB tight-lipped on royal proclamation issue, Zahid meeting
Article:
SEREMBAN: Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim remained tight-lipped over an alleged proclamation seeking the removal of state ruler Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.
Ismail also declined to comment on the outcome of his meeting with Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi and three party vice-presidents on Thursday.
He merely smiled at reporters before entering his official vehicle and driving off after launching the Negri Sembilan Community Programme at his official residence today.
The meeting between Ismail and Zahid took place at 4pm in a private room during the 2026 UMNO General Assembly at the World Trade Centre (WTC) in Kuala Lumpur.
The meeting followed
Zahid's earlier statement seeking clarification from Ismai
l regarding claims that the menteri besar was forced to sign a proclamation document to depose Tuanku Muhriz at Istana Laguna Biru in Port Dickson on Aug 3.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Don't take law into own hands over Rohingya issue, cops warn
Article:
BACHOK: Police have warned the public, including social media influencers, against taking matters into their own hands over issues involving the Rohingya community and its settlements.
Bukit Aman Crime Prevention and Community Safety Department director Datuk Noor Hisam Nordin said such matters should be left to the authorities, including the police and Immigration Department.
"If there is any confusion or incident that requires action from the authorities, including identifying Rohingya settlements, report it to the police.
"Let the authorities handle these issues. We see a lot of provocations or negative messages regarding the Rohingya on social media right now," he said at a press conference at Universiti Malaysia Kelantan today.
Also present were Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat and UMK vice-chancellor Datuk Prof Dr Arham Abdullah.
Hisam said individuals should not allow emotions to drive them to overstep boundaries or disrupt public order.
"It is our duty as the police to ensure public peace. Regardless of the issue, whether it involves race, ethnicity or foreign nationals, contact the police if you have any information.
"Do not attempt to make things viral, including Rohingya settlements, thinking that authorities will act faster that way," he said.
He said taking matters into their own hands could lead to negative outcomes.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Govt opens door to more vehicle inspection centres: Anthony Loke
Article:
SUNGAI BULOH: The government wants to see more MV15 vehicle inspection centres opened nationwide to improve access for vehicle owners, Transport Minister Anthony Loke said.
He said the government will not limit the number of operators for MV15 inspection centres.
Any company that meets the stipulated requirements is welcome to apply for a licence.
"We want to see more centres like this opened throughout the country so that people in every state can enjoy the same access," Loke said at the launch of Carsome Academy's MV15 inspection centre today
Opening the market to more operators will give vehicle owners greater choice and a more convenient experience, he added.
MV15 inspections are required for private vehicles undergoing a change of ownership.
He said the government had moved from a single-operator concession system to a multi-operator licensing system following the expiry of the previous concession on Aug 31, 2024.
Loke also said inspection fees at all licensed centres remained standardised and regulated by the government, meaning operators could not compete on price.
"Therefore, no operator can compete through pricing. Competition can only take place through service quality, transparency and efficiency," he said.
The newly-launched Sungai Buloh centre, Malaysia's first MV15 inspection centre backed by an automotive training institution, can handle up to 90 inspections a day and about 2,300 inspections a month.
The centre integrates vehicle inspection services with Carsome Academy's technical and vocational education and training programmes, with inspections conducted by inspectors accredited under the Malaysian Skills Certificate Level Three in Motor Vehicle Inspection.
Carsome said customers can make appointments digitally, while inspection records and results are transmitted directly to systems connected to the Road Transport Department (JPJ).
The company said it has consistently recorded a 99 per cent first-time pass rate for vehicles undergoing inspections in accordance with JPJ requirements.
Carsome Group co-founder and Carsome Academy chief executive officer Teoh Jiun Ee said the centre would help develop skilled inspectors, maintain high inspection standards and strengthen confidence in the vehicle ownership transfer process.
"At the same time, it provides aspiring automotive professionals with opportunities to gain practical industry experience through Carsome Academy," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sewage turns Redang waterway black, foul-smelling
Article:
KUALA NERUS: Behind the pristine beauty of Pulau Redang, one of the country's renowned tourist destinations, lies a growing environmental concern at Pantai Panjang, where a once-clear waterway has turned black and emits a foul odour.
The pollution is believed to be linked to sewage overflow from nearby resorts, with wastewater flowing into a drainage channel and potentially reaching the sea, particularly during high tides and rough monsoon conditions.
A survey found that the sewage systems built by resort operators in the area lacked proper treatment facilities, and existing holding tanks were not considered a wastewater treatment method.
More concerning, the waterway was once a source of clean water and a bathing spot for villagers living around Pulau Redang.
Residents said the situation was vastly different in the 1990s, when the stream formed by water flowing down from the hills was still clear.
Today, the water has not only changed colour but also emits a foul smell, raising concerns over environmental pollution and its impact on marine life.
Terengganu Department of Environment (DOE) director Hamzah Mohamad said the holding tanks used in the area were not a sewage treatment method, adding that every facility should have its own treatment system that complies with the prescribed standards.
"Actually, the holding tank is not a treatment method. Under the regulations, facilities here must have a main treatment system and comply with the standards we have set.
"Under the Environmental Quality (Sewage) Regulations 2009, all facilities within marine park areas must comply with Standard A. So, it is rather strange when we look at the quality of the treated water here because there is no treatment at all," he said.
He said this when commenting on the sewage system at Pantai Panjang, Pulau Redang.
Meanwhile, Terengganu Tourism, Culture, Environment and Climate Change Committee chairman Datuk Razali Idris said the issue of wastewater discharge from resorts in the area had persisted for several years, despite various efforts to resolve it.
"If I am not mistaken, I came here two years ago, and the same problem was happening even though we had tried our best. However, we will continue looking for a solution to the wastewater problem.
"We have to take responsibility for the wastewater discharged by the hotels around here," he said.
Razali said the state government had previously allocated RM100,000 to temporarily divert the water flow, but the same problem had resurfaced.
He said a contractor had expressed willingness to invest in constructing and managing a sewage treatment plant in the area.
The proposal is expected to address wastewater discharge from resorts around Pantai Panjang more comprehensively and effectively.
Meanwhile, resident Maarop Ismail, 60, urged all parties, including resort operators, not to focus solely on profits from the tourism sector but also to take responsibility for preserving Pulau Redang's environment.
"I hope this problem can be resolved. All the resorts discharging sewage into the river should not just think about making money, but also address the pollution affecting Redang's beaches.
"If possible, we do not want this to become a source of disease in the future," he said.
To address the problem, the developer has reportedly agreed to bear RM5.7 million in costs to build a sewage treatment plant on a government reserve land at Pantai Panjang.
However, the proposal is subject to the state government's approval, with the developer seeking a parcel of land in exchange for about five acres on the island it has applied for.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Johor's Tanjung Pelepas Port under cyberattack, launches system clean-up
Article:
jashadiqe@nst.com.my
JOHOR BARU: The Tanjung Pelepas Port (PTP), one of the world's busiest container transhipment hubs, was forced to temporarily suspend terminal operations after a cyberattack disrupted its operating systems last week.
Lloyd's List, a leading global maritime industry publication, reported that the cybersecurity attack was detected at 11.34pm on Sept 9.
This prompted PTP to isolate the affected systems and suspend operations as a precaution while recovery efforts began.
The terminal began a controlled resumption of operations on Sept 10, including manual processing at its gates for laden and empty export containers.
The New Straits Times contacted PTP, however, the port management declined to comment on the incident.
Meanwhile, reliable sources within PTP told Business Times that the hackers had given the port a deadline to contact them but did not demand a ransom.
The sources said PTP adopted a strict no-negotiation stance towards the hackers.
Its information technology team was conducting a comprehensive "clean sweep" of its systems as part of the recovery and security measures.
PTP is also progressively restoring affected systems while ensuring operations are not compromised further.
The cyberattack is significant given PTP's role as a major regional transhipment hub.
The wider Johor port complex handled a record 15.1 million 20-foot equivalent units (TEUs) in 2025, with more than 14 million TEUs moving through PTP alone.
In laymen terms, Johor's ports handled a record 15.1 million container units in 2025, with PTP accounting for more than 14 million.
According to Lloyd's List, Maersk - one of PTP's major customers - said it was working closely with the terminal and managing the operational impact.
"While some vessels may experience delays, recovery efforts are progressing well," Lloyd's List quoted a Maersk spokesperson.
It added that its priority was to minimise disruption to customers and support the normalisation of supply chains, while its vessel tracking showed limited operational impact, with scheduled containership arrivals and departures largely continuing, although some movements were affected.
The cyber incident comes as ports and shipping operators face growing exposure to cyberattacks because of their reliance on interconnected digital systems for vessel scheduling, container tracking, gate operations and yard management.
The maritime sector has previously been hit by major cyberattacks, including the 2017 NotPetya attack that severely disrupted Maersk's global operations.
A ransomware group known as Direwolf has separately listed PTP on its leak site, claiming an attack, but the claim has not been independently verified and PTP has not publicly attributed the incident to the group.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: M & A Equity not involved in Next Lion, puts Sean Yap on administrative leave
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: M & A Equity Holdings Bhd has put the chief executive officer of its asset management unit on administrative leave with effect from Sept 8 until further notice, as a precautionary measure, to facilitate an independent review of his involvement in Next Lion Holdings Ltd.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the stockbroking firm said that Sean Yap Shon Leong's involvement in Next Lion and its subsidiaries was undertaken solely in his personal capacity and not on behalf of the group.
"This measure should not, in itself, be construed as a determination or admission of any wrongdoing on the part of Yap," it said. The CEO of M & A Asset Management Sdn Bhd (MAAM) is the sole shareholder and a director of Next Lion.
In addition, M & A Equity said the administrative leave is not expected to have any material impact on the business or operations of the company.
"Concurrently, the board has also notified the Securities Commission Malaysia of Yap's involvement in Next Lion and the independent review being undertaken by the board in relation to the matter," it added.
Next Lion holds a 50 per cent stake in MYEG Ventures Sdn Bhd, of which Zetrix AI Bhd was looking to acquire for RM130 million. The purchase consideration was to be satisfied via cash and share issuances of up to 360.6 million shares.
MyEG Ventures holds a 51 per cent interest in MyEG Philippines Ltd. However, barely three days after the initial announcement on Sept 1, Zetrix aborted the proposed transaction, attributing the decision to fluctuations in its share price.
M & A Equity said Yap's involvement in Next Lion and its group of companies was not related to MAAM. The company said Next Lion and its group of companies are not subsidiaries, associated companies, joint ventures or investee companies of M & A Equity.
"Neither M & A Equity nor MAAM is a party to, or has any involvement in, the transactions involving Next Lion Group referred to in the article," it said in a filing with Bursa Malaysia today, referring to two articles published by an English-language publication.
M & A Equity also said Yap was not acting for or on behalf of, and had not been authorised to represent any companies within the group in relation to the transactions or arrangements.
The company clarified that it had not provided any funding, financial assistance, guarantee, undertaking or support to Next Lion or in connection with the transactions referred to in the reports.
"The matters referred to in the article do not have any financial or operational impact on M & A Equity," it said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Penang Gerakan calls for probe into alleged assault on primary student
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Gerakan has called on the Penang Education Department to investigate an alleged assault involving a 9-year-old primary school pupil.
Penang Gerakan public complaints bureau chief Andrew Ooi said the complaint involved a pupil from a Chinese primary school in the southwest district who sustained bruising to his left back and arm after being hit by a teacher.
"We are not here to determine who is guilty or who is right or wrong. That is for the relevant authorities to investigate," he told reporters today.
Ooi said the incident, reported to the bureau on Sept 8, should not be dismissed as an ordinary disciplinary matter if a child was allegedly left with physical injuries.
He said that while teachers had a responsibility to discipline pupils, such action must remain within proper boundaries and should not result in physical injury.
Ooi also cautioned against condemning teachers as a whole, acknowledging that educators faced heavy workloads, administrative responsibilities, classroom management challenges and, in some schools, manpower shortages.
He, however, said such pressures could not justify taking anger out on pupils.
Ooi called on the Education Ministry to address systemic issues, including concerns involving bullying, student mental health and violence.
He proposed regular training for teachers covering student and classroom management, anger and stress management, conflict management, child protection, appropriate disciplinary methods, mental-health awareness and counselling support.
At the Penang Education Department today, Ooi said the bureau sought an impartial investigation, a clear explanation for the parents and protection for the child's welfare and safety.
He also urged authorities to ensure the child and his family were not subjected to retaliation, intimidation or discrimination for lodging the complaint.
"A child has the right to be disciplined. But a child also has the right to be safe, respected and protected at school," he added.
The identities of the pupil, teacher and school were withheld to protect the child.
The New Straits Times has contacted state Education Department director Mohamad Dziauddin Mat Saad for comment.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Data centres must deliver more than investment: Deputy minister, MIDA
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has recorded RM385.7 billion in data centre-related investments from 2021 to the first half of 2026.
However, the government wants the sector's growth to translate into more local businesses, skilled jobs and technology capabilities.
Deputy Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Sim Tze Tzin said Malaysia's next phase of digital infrastructure development must focus on creating economic value from the capacity being built.
"As the scale and pace of investment increase, our priorities must evolve with the industry.
"The next phase is about what that capacity delivers - AI adoption, home-grown innovation, skilled talent and higher-value jobs," he said at Data Centre Nexus (DCN) 2026 today.
"We want Malaysia recognised as a competitive, resilient and sustainable digital hub, where infrastructure, technology, talent and innovation converge to create high-value economic activity," he added.
Malaysian Investment Development Authority (MIDA) chairman Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Abdul Aziz said the benefits of data-centre investments should extend beyond the facilities themselves.
"Data centres are a critical driver of our digital and compute economy, but their true measure of success lies well beyond the data halls themselves," he said.
MIDA chief executive officer Datuk Sikh Shamsul Ibrahim Sikh Abdul Majid said the focus was onbuilding a sustainable ecosystem while managingthe sector's energy, water and land requirements.
"In the end, our goal is simple: we do not just want more data centres in Malaysia. We want an ecosystem that is competitive, innovative and sustainable."
DCN 2026 brought together operators, technology firms, government agencies, financial institutions and local suppliers.
Its business-matching session involved 14 data-centre companies and 51 Malaysian vendors, up from eight and 17 respectively at the inaugural event in 2025.
The event also focused on AI infrastructure, sustainability, local supply chains and digital technology adoption. Malaysia's data-centre electricity demand is projected to exceed 5,000MW by 2035.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 3 Penang heritage sites offer free entry for two days
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Three heritage sites in Penang will offer free entry for two days from tomorrow in conjunction with the fifth anniversary of Penang Hill's recognition as a Unesco Biosphere Reserve and Malaysia Day.
State Tourism and Creative Economy Committee chairman Wong Hon Wai said the three sites were the Penang State Automotive Gallery, Fort Cornwallis and the Penang State Museum.
"The public and tourists from Malaysia and abroad are welcome to take this opportunity to explore history, appreciate the state's heritage, gain a deeper understanding of Penang's past and discover Malaysia's rich and diverse cultural heritage," he said in a statement today.
He said free admission to the Automotive Gallery and Fort Cornwallis had also been extended until October, giving the public more time to visit the two sites.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: FGV appoints independent firm for forensic audit
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Federal Land Development Authority's (Felda) subsidiary, FGV Holdings Bhd, has appointed an independent audit firm to conduct a forensic audit regarding specific matters involving an entity with corporate ties to the group.
In a press statement, Felda noted that the process of appointing independent audit firms is actively being carried out for several other subsidiaries.
"This appointment is carried out in line with the recommendations of the Prime Minister, the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC), and the Special Committee on the Direction of Felda 2030.
"This step is specifically designed to improve the governance of the FeldaGroup for the sustainability of the agency," it said.
It stressed that Felda will continue to review the need to appoint an independent audit firm to conduct a professional and comprehensive forensic audit on Felda and all organisations under the Felda Group.
For the record, the forensic audit initiative against Felda has been implemented since 2019.
Felda had previously appointed Ernst & Young (EY), and the findings of the audit report were presented in Parliament through the Felda White Paper in 2020.
"The implementation of this latest audit reflects the ongoing commitment of Felda Group management to strengthen governance, accountability, transparency and compliance at all levels of operation.
"Felda remains steadfast in its stance to ensure the interests of the organisation and the well-being of the settlers are always protected and preserved," it added.– BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Toddler attack: 3 dogs yet to be caught in Johor
Article:
BATU PAHAT: Fears over stray dogs have resurfaced in Kampung Tambak, Peserai, after about 10 dogs were spotted roaming near the home of a toddler mauled last week.
However, three of the five dogs that attacked two-year-old Nur Haira Wafiqah Mohammad Hamizi have yet to be caught and remain in the area.
The dogs were seen running through an oil palm smallholding behind the toddler's grandfather's house at about 11am today, with residents saying some appeared to be fighting.
A resident who identified herself as Nur, 23, said
authorities had caught seven dogs
following the attack.
"That is worrying because the presence of other stray dogs could cause more problems and disturb residents. We do not want what happened to my niece to happen again," she said.
Nur Haira was attacked by dogs last week and
remains warded
at Sultanah Aminah Hospital.
Nur said the toddler was expected to undergo reconstructive surgery on her head and face as her injuries could not be treated through conventional treatment.
She said Nur Haira was now breathing on her own without respiratory support and had opened her eyes.
"Doctors are still monitoring her condition and giving her pain medication. We hope people will pray for her speedy recovery," she said.
A check at the scene found that authorities had also placed traps to catch the remaining three dogs believed to have attacked the toddler.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anthony Loke urges PH council meeting amid political uncertainty
Article:
SUNGAI BULOH: DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke will ask Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to convene a Pakatan Harapan (PH) presidential council meeting to review recent political developments amid concerns over political certainty and stability.
Loke, who is also Transport Minister, said recent statements by component parties in the unity government suggested they were not moving in the same direction, potentially undermining confidence among investors and the public.
He was responding to a question on Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi's challenge to the party's critics to either call a general election or table a vote of no confidence in Parliament.
"We view all this development with concern and with our serious consideration. I will definitely ask the Prime Minister to have a presidential council meeting in PH to review and to discuss the latest development.
"Some of the statements made are, of course, not good in terms of the political certainty and political stability in the country that the component parties in the government seems to be not heading in the same direction," Loke said.
He was speaking after the launch of Carsome's Malaysia's first academy-backed MV15 inspection centre.
"This is something which I think the prime minister must clarify with all component parties.
"I would like to suggest to the prime minister, once he is back from his overseas trip, to convene a presidential council meeting of PH," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fun picnic trip turns fatal at Rompin waterfall
Article:
ROMPIN: A picnic outing for nine friends at the Air Leleh waterfall in Bukit Ibam ended in tragedy when one of them drowned yesterday.
The body of Muhammad Azreen Othman, 25, was found by divers at 8.50am today at a depth of 12 metres, six metres from where he was last seen.
District police chief Superintendent Sharif Shai Sharif Mondoi said Azreen and eight friends, including five women from Felda Keratong, had gone to the waterfall for a picnic at 2pm yesterday.
"They entered the water 30 minutes later. The victim remained in the water alone while his friends climbed onto the banks to rest at 3.30pm.
"All of them were in the water about 4pm before the victim, who was clinging to a rope tied between trees across the water, lost his grip and was swept away by the strong current towards a rapid," he said in a statement today.
Sharif Shai said two of Azreen's friends managed to grab his hands, but the strong current and slippery riverbed swept him away.
He said a picnicker alerted the Bukit Ibam police station at 5.40pm, prompting a search and rescue operation at 6pm.
"The search operation involved Civil Defence Force personnel and Fire and Rescue Department divers. Two divers entered the water at 8.30am today and found the body 20 minutes later.
"The body was taken to Muadzam Shah Hospital at 9.55am for a post-mortem examination. The case has been classified as sudden death," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: GXBank gets IFC backstop for RM470mil MSME lending push
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: GXBank has secured up to US$4.95 million (RM21 million) in first-loss coverage from the International Finance Corp (IFC), which the bank calls the first risk-sharing partnership of its kind for a Malaysian digital bank.
The facility aims to help GXBank expand lending to underserved micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), supporting a target loan portfolio of up to US$110 million (RM470 million).
IFC will absorb initial losses on eligible loans, allowing GXBank to lend to "thin-file" businesses that lack conventional credit histories or collateral, the bank said in a statement.
The arrangement could also improve GXBank's capital efficiency by reducing the risk-weighted capital needed for the covered loans under Bank Negara Malaysia rules, giving it more balance-sheet room to expand automated lending.
GXBank said 15,000 MSMEs have opened digital accounts, with more than 5,000 loan drawdowns so far.
Separately, it has approved RM27 million in Credit Guarantee Corporation Malaysia-backed facilities since March, while maximum credit limits for expanding businesses have been raised to RM350,000 from RM150,000.
The bank has also completed a proof-of-concept with fintech startup Finory to automate onboarding for micro-traders using local-authority business licences.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pasir Gudang API hits 152 as haze blankets parts of Johor
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Haze blanketed parts of Johor today, with Pasir Gudang recording an Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 152, placing it in the unhealthy category.
Larkin was also in the unhealthy category, with an API reading of 150, while Pengerang recorded 114.
Tangkak recorded 106, also in the unhealthy category, while Kluang and Kota Tinggi registered 96 and 91, respectively, both at moderate levels.
Batu Pahat recorded 85, while Segamat stood at 84.
Meanwhile, Johor Health and Environment Committee chairman Ling Tian Soon said the state Environment Department (DoE) was monitoring air quality hourly and would take action according to the haze situation.
He said the department was closely monitoring readings at all air-quality monitoring stations as several areas recorded unhealthy levels.
Fine airborne particles measuring 2.5 micrometres or smaller, which can penetrate deep into the lungs, were the main pollutant recorded at all monitoring stations.s
An API reading of 101 to 150 is classified as unhealthy, triggering measures including stopping all outdoor activities involving students and intensifying patrols at fire-prone areas and construction sites.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Petronas, PTT extends gas production from Malaysia-Thailand JDA for another 35 years
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Petroliam Nasional Bhd's (Petronas) unit Petronas Carigali Sdn Bhd, together with the subsidiaries of Thailand's PTT have secured a new 35-year production sharing contract (PSC) for a gas-producing block in the Malaysia-Thailand Joint Development Area (MTJDA).
In a statement, Petronas said the contract for Block A-18-01 was signed by Petronas Carigali's unit PC JDA Ltd, and PTT's subsidiaries PTTEP JDX Thailand Ltd Co and PTTEP JDX Thailand (JDA) Ltd, following approvals from the Malaysian and Thai governments.
The new contract extends development of the existing Block A-18 beyond the current contract's expiry on April 20, 2029 and incorporates an adjacent exploration area with additional resource potential.
The parties also signed a gas sales agreement with their parent companies, Petronas and PTT, to support continued gas supplies from the block to both countries.
Starting Jan 1, the new PSC for Block A-18-01 encompasses both the existing Block A-18 area and the additional new area, for 35 years.
Spanning about 7,250 square kilometres, the MTJDA comprises Blocks A-18-01 and B-17-01, which have a combined natural gas production capacity of around 700 million standard cubic feet per day with equal distribution to Malaysia and Thailand.
Block A-18-01 comprises the Cakerawala, Bumi, Suriya, Bulan, South Bulan, Senja, East Bumi, Samudra and Wira gas fields, including the open area.
Meanwhile,Block B-17-01 comprises the Muda, Tapi, Tanjung, Amarit, Jengka, Melati and Andalas gas fields.
PC JDA director Ainoor Abizzurin Abdullah said the approval of the new PSC ushers in the next phase of development for Block A-18-01, reflecting the enduring resolve and strong collaboration between Malaysia and Thailand.
"As a key source of natural gas and condensate for both countries, this milestone reinforces our shared commitment to maximise value through enhanced resource monetisation and operational synergies," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bintulu Port returns to Sarawak after 48 years
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bintulu Port has officially returned to Sarawak's jurisdiction after 48 years under the federal government's regulatory framework.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, Bintulu Port Holdings Bhd (BPHB) said the transition took effect on Sept 1 following the coming into force of two federal laws.
The laws are the Declaration of an Area in the Bintulu District to be a Federal Port (Repeal) Act 2024 and the Bintulu Port Authority (Dissolution) Act 2024.
Bintulu Port was declared a federal port in 1978 and became operational in 1983. It subsequently grew into the largest container port in Sabah and Sarawak, and Malaysia's sole LNG export gateway.
BPHB's unit Bintulu Port Sdn Bhd will continue to operate, manage and develop the port under Sarawak's regulatory framework.
The operations are governed by a heads of agreement dated July 27 between the Sarawak government, Bintulu Port Authority (Sarawak) and BPSB, pending the execution of a port operation concession agreement.
BPHB said the Sarawak Infrastructure and Port Development Ministry had notified it on June 23 that the state government had approved in principle its appointment as the approved port operator under Section 12(2)(a) of the Port Authorities Ordinance, 1961.
The transition also ends the previous federal operating arrangements.
BPHB said the privatisation agreement dated Dec 31, 1992, the fourth interim agreement dated Dec 22, 2025, and related federal arrangements ceased to have effect from Sept 1.
Under a tripartite agreement dated June 21, Sarawak and BPSB also agreed to release the federal government from claims arising from or connected to the privatisation agreement.
BPHB said it would work with the Sarawak government, BPA Sarawak and relevant authorities to ensure a smooth transition and continuity of port operations.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Umno lacks numbers to destabilise unity government, says analyst
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Umno does not appear to have sufficient political strength to destabilise the unity government despite party president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi's challenge to the administration, an analyst said.
Universiti Teknologi Malaysia (UTM) Faculty of Social Sciences and Humanities director Associate Professor Dr Mazlan Ali said if Umno intended to withdraw its support, the party could utilise several established democratic avenues.
Mazlan said Pasir Gudang member of parliament Hassan Abdul Karim had outlined the most viable options for Zahid to challenge the unity hovernment without waiting for Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to expel Umno from the coalition.
"From a parliamentary democracy perspective, Hassan's suggestion is the best option if Umno truly wants to withdraw from the government because it no longer supports the administration.
"First, because Umno no longer has confidence in this unity government, they can withdraw," Mazlan said when contacted.
Mazlan said Umno ministers could also resign if they disagreed with the prime minister's stance, adhering to the principle of collective cabinet responsibility.
"Any minister who disagrees with the prime minister can either be dismissed by the prime minister or choose to resign. However, resigning is the better option.
"Another option is to table a motion in Parliament to test whether the current prime minister still commands majority support," he said.
However, Mazlan noted that Umno and Barisan Nasional appeared unconfident in their ability to collapse the unity government by withdrawing support.
"Currently, support for the prime minister stands at 153 MPs. Excluding three PKR MPs, that leaves 150. Even if BN exits, there are still 120 MPs, which remains a simple majority government," he said.
Mazlan added that support for Anwar could increase if independent MPs such as Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman backed the government, alongside six Bersatu MPs who previously declared support.
"That could bring support for Anwar to nearly 127 MPs if these parties back him. Even without them, it remains at 120," he said.
The six Bersatu MPs who previously declared support for Anwar are Datuk Syed Abu Hussin Hafiz Syed Abdul Fasal (Bukit Gantang), Datuk Dr Suhaili Abdul Rahman (Labuan), Zahari Kechik (Jeli), Mohd Azizi Abu Naim (Gua Musang), Datuk Iskandar Dzulkarnain Abdul Khalid (Kuala Kangsar), and Datuk Dr Zulkafperi Hanapi (Tanjong Karang).
Mazlan said the unity government's position would only be at risk if support from Sabah and Sarawak were withdrawn.
However, he noted that Anwar's relationship with Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Abang Openg and Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor remained strong.
"As long as this support remains intact, I do not believe Umno has the confidence to destabilise the government.
"Zahid's statements at the 2026 Umno General Assembly were primarily intended to reassure delegates and unite the party's leaders and members," Mazlan said.
Hassan previously outlined
three options
for Zahid: withdrawing Umno and BN MP support, having Umno ministers resign from Cabinet, or tabling a vote of no confidence against the prime minister when Parliament reconvenes on Oct 5.
Umno had previously issued an ultimatum to the unity government to either seek a fresh mandate through the 16th General Election (GE16) or formally remove the party from the coalition.
Meanwhile, Nusantara Academy for Strategic Research senior fellow Azmi Hassan said that while the three options were theoretically open to Umno MPs, they could not be executed while BN remained in the unity government,
Azmi noted that Zahid had pledged to support Anwar until Parliament was dissolved.
"Under current circumstances, these three options are technically available but will not be carried out.
"Doing so would violate Zahid's promise to the prime minister," Azmi said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kelantan quadruplets leave home for UTHM in Johor
Article:
BATU PAHAT: Four identical brothers from Kelantan have begun their university journey together, enrolling in the same degree programme at Universiti Tun Hussein Onn Malaysia (UTHM) today.
The 23-year-old quadruplets — Amir Muttaqin, Aniq Muttaqin, Abid Muttaqin and Adib Muttaqin Md Khairuddin — were among 3,302 students registering for the 2026/2027 academic session.
All four chose the Bachelor of Real Estate Management (Honours) programme at UTHM's Faculty of Technology Management and Business, having already obtained Certificates in Property Valuation from the National Institute of Valuation.
"We had always wanted to pursue a degree in real estate management, which is why we chose UTHM.
"We are happy and excited to have the opportunity to continue our studies at university," they said after registering at the UTHM campus in Parit Raja here.
For Abid, however, the excitement came with a tinge of sadness and nerves as the brothers had to leave their family and travel far from Kelantan for the first time as university students.
"It is exciting to have made it to degree level, but we are also sad to leave our family.
"At the same time, it is a little nerve-racking because this is our first university experience and we are now far from home," he said.
Being quadruplets, however, could give them an advantage in navigating university life, particularly when it came to studying and keeping each other on track.
"We can study and revise together, remind each other about classes and assignments, and help one another while living at the college," he said.
UTHM vice-chancellor Professor Dr Mas Fawzi Mohd Ali said the new intake comprised 1,885 male and 1,417 female students across eight faculties.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Saifuddin Nasution: Second multi-purpose mission ship under construction in Turkiye to be completed by end‑2027
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 14 — The second Multi-Purpose Mission Ship (MPMS), which is currently under construction in Turkiye, is expected to be completed and handed over to the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) by the end of next year, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
He said the first MPMS vessel was expected to arrive in March next year, a month before the Langkawi International Maritime and Aerospace Exhibition (LIMA).
“If you recall, two years ago, when President (Recep Tayyip) Erdogan came here, we signed an agreement to purchase one vessel. In less than two years, it is now ready.
“Compared with (if) we were to build it ourselves, there have been various cases where vessels were not completed, funds were exhausted and all sorts of other issues. This has given the Home Ministry confidence that it made the right decision, with a shorter construction period and a reasonable price,” he told the media after attending the Home Ministry’s monthly assembly here today.
Saifuddin Nasution said he would travel to Istanbul, Turkiye, at the end of this month to personally inspect the progress of the vessel’s construction.
He said the vessel’s construction was progressing ahead of schedule, further convincing the ministry that its decision was the right one in terms of the construction period and reasonable price.
The development of the vessel is another important step in efforts to strengthen the capabilities of the MMEA, particularly in addressing an increasingly complex maritime security environment.
In a related development, the ministry will evaluate an offer for a second offshore patrol vessel previously operated by the United States Coast Guard (USCG), based on its seaworthiness and repair costs.
Saifuddin Nasution said the evaluation would be based on a report by Home Ministry secretary-general Datuk Dr Awang Alik Jeman following an inspection conducted with MMEA experts, engineers and officers.
“They made the offer, but we have to satisfy ourselves (as to whether) it is seaworthy or not. So I tasked the secretary-general to go and inspect it, then submit a report to me,” he said.
He said Malaysia had previously received its first offshore patrol vessel from the USCG, which is now stationed in Kota Kinabalu, Sabah.
He added that cooperation with the USCG had been established since the formation of the MMEA and covered areas such as asset contributions, training, joint operations and intelligence sharing.
“If its seaworthiness is low and the cost to us is even higher, that would be a burden. We will not agree to it,” he said.
The government previously acquired the KM BENDAHARA offshore patrol vessel through the United States Foreign Military Sales (FMS) programme, and it was officially handed over to the MMEA on Sept 5, 2025, in Baltimore, United States. — Bernama

Title: Carried by teenager porter, rescued Croatian climber says Kinabalu ordeal broke his heart
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 14 — Croatian climber Mauro Persic has expressed regret over the risks he took after being found injured and alone on Mount Kinabalu for eight days, but said the ordeal strengthened his faith in human compassion.
Persic, 46, said the rescue operation was a humbling experience, particularly when rescuers and porters had to carry him down because he was too weak and injured to continue on his own,
Berita Harian
reported.
One of the moments that struck him most was being carried by a porter estimated to be about 15 years old.
“One of the porters was so young, perhaps 15 years (old), I could feel each impact of his legs and knees, it broke my heart that I'm contributing to this
“Was it all worth it? I don’t know. Probably not. Broken body. 40 people risking their lives to save one. But still, I’ve seen the very best of humanity showing up these days; generosity, kindness and care,” he wrote in a Facebook post.
He added that rescuers brought him food, chocolate and snacks, gathered around campfires, shared jokes and kept him company while efforts were made to bring him down safely.
The Croatian climber, who was rescued last week in an operation involving multiple agencies, sustained injuries to his right leg and ribs, as well as minor wounds to his hands during the incident.

Title: Anthony Loke calls for Pakatan Presidential Council meeting to discuss recent political developments after Umno assembly
Article:
SUNGAI BULOH, Sept 14 — DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke said he will propose to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim that the Pakatan Harapan (PH) Presidential Council convene to discuss recent political developments following statements made at the Umno General Assembly.
He said the recent statements raised concerns regarding political certainty and stability, which could affect investor and public confidence in the country.
Loke said the developments were viewed with concern and serious consideration, adding that he would request Anwar, who is PH chairman, to call for a Presidential Council meeting to review and discuss the latest developments upon his return from his overseas trip.
“Some of the statements made are of course not good in terms of political certainty and political stability in the country, as component parties in the government seem to not be heading in the same direction.
“So this is something which would not give much confidence to investors and to the public. The Prime Minister must also make this clear with all component parties,” the Transport Minister said.
Loke said this when met by reporters after officiating the CARSOME Academy M.V.15 Vehicle Inspection Centre at the CARSOME Dealer Hub here.
He was responding to media queries on remarks made by Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi in his winding-up speech at the recently concluded Umno assembly, which touched on Barisan Nasional’s (BN) position in the Unity Government.
On whether PH would seek clarification on BN’s position or the challenges issued by the Umno leadership, Loke maintained that any official top-level response should come directly from the Prime Minister. — Bernama

Title: Penang Port Commission, PPSB to offer free ferry services on Malaysia Day
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 14 — The Penang Port Commission (SPPP) and Penang Port Sdn Bhd (PPSB) are offering free ferry services to Malaysians on September 16 in conjunction with Malaysia Day celebrations and the Keretapi Sarong Festival.
SPPP chairman Datuk Yeoh Soon Hin said the offer applies to trips from both ferry terminals, Pangkalan Sultan Abdul Halim (PSAH) in Seberang Perai and Pangkalan Raja Tun Uda (PRTU) here, in accordance with the existing service schedule.
“With this free ferry service offer, I hope to alleviate the financial burden on Malaysians while providing an opportunity to celebrate Malaysia Day and participate in the Keretapi Sarong Festival in a meaningful way,” he said in a statement today.
He noted that commuters would enjoy savings of RM2 per one-way trip for pedestrians and RM2.50 for two-wheeled vehicle users.
According to him, during last year’s Malaysia Day celebration, a total of 10,094 pedestrians and 1,909 two-wheeled vehicles utilised the ferry service for round trips.
Yeoh added that these figures contributed to the overall annual total of 3,131,131 pedestrians and 784,065 two-wheeled vehicles recorded in 2025.
He said the initiative also aims to help reduce traffic congestion in Penang, in addition to encouraging the use of more sustainable and efficient public transportation. — Bernama

Title: Chief of Defence Force: MAF proposes reinstating multi‑agency border‑security framework used under former national task force
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 14 — The Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) has submitted a proposal to the National Security Council (NSC) to reinstate a multi-agency operational framework modelled on the National Task Force (NTF) to bolster national border security.
Chief of Defence Force Gen Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman said the proposal, submitted through the National Operational Management Committee, would bring together various agencies including the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA), the Royal Malaysian Customs Department (JKDM), and the Immigration Department of Malaysia (JIM).
He said the strategic coordination of enforcement agencies has proven more effective in addressing security vulnerabilities along the country’s land and maritime borders.
“We executed this (integrated operation) previously via the NTF during the Covid-19 pandemic, and it proved effective in coordinating multi-agency efforts before the mechanism was changed for specific reasons.
“Therefore, I believe elements of that approach should be reinstated, even if not on a large scale, to address current security challenges and vulnerabilities,” he said during a Special Media Interview with the Chief of Defence Forces in conjunction with the 93rd MAF Day at Wisma Pertahanan here today.
Malek Razak said the MAF conducts round-the-clock surveillance along the national border and regularly detains intruders, though not all cases are reported to the media.
“Malaysia also maintains close cooperation with neighbouring countries such as Thailand and Indonesia to tackle cross-border security issues through intelligence sharing,” he explained.
Touching on integrity issues, he said the main measure against corruption at the border is instilling integrity and high moral values among personnel.
The NTF, was established to carry out Op Benteng to curb the influx of illegal immigrants during the pandemic in 2020, was officially disbanded on December 31, 2022. — Bernama

Title: Two‑year‑old mauled by stray dogs in Batu Pahat to undergo reconstructive surgery
Article:
BATU PAHAT, Sept 14 — A two-year-old girl mauled by stray dogs outside her grandmother’s home in Kampung Tambak, Peserai, is expected to undergo reconstructive surgery soon as she continues to fight for her life.
Nur Haira Wafiqah Mohammad Hamizi was critically injured in the Sept 6 attack by five dogs, suffering severe head and facial wounds.
As reported by
Berita Harian
, Haira’s aunt, who wished to be identified only as Nur, 23, said doctors had informed the child’s parents that reconstructive surgery was the best option given the extent of her injuries.
“We were told that ordinary treatment or surgery would not be suitable. Haira can now breathe on her own without respiratory support. She has also opened her eyes, though there is no response yet. The medical team is still monitoring her condition, and we ask everyone to pray for her recovery,” she said.
Nur also told
BH
that before all the dogs involved in the attack could be captured, villagers in Kampung Tambak, Peserai, were confronted by another pack of strays.
She said around 10 dogs were spotted in an oil palm plantation behind the victim’s grandfather’s house, and their presence was even recorded on video before they disappeared.
“I believe 10 other dogs appeared at the plantation around 11am today. Previously, the authorities caught seven dogs, including five puppies, which attacked Haira. Three more have yet to be captured and are still roaming near the house.
“Now another pack of strays has emerged, raising fears they could cause further problems and disturb residents. We do not want a repeat of what happened to my niece,” she said.

Title: Free entry to three Penang heritage sites for two days starting tomorrow in conjunction with Malaysia Day
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 14 — Three heritage sites in Penang will offer free entry for two days from tomorrow in conjunction with the fifth anniversary of Penang Hill’s recognition as a Unesco Biosphere Reserve and Malaysia Day.
State Tourism and Creative Economy Committee chairman Wong Hon Wai said the three sites are the Penang State Automotive Gallery, Fort Cornwallis and the Penang State Museum.
“The public and tourists from Malaysia and abroad, are welcome to take this opportunity to explore history, appreciate the state’s heritage, gain a deeper understanding of Penang’s past and discover Malaysia’s rich and diverse cultural heritage,” he said in a statement today.
He said free admission to the Automotive Gallery and Fort Cornwallis had also been extended until October, giving the public more time to visit the two sites. — Bernama

Title: Federal Court hears PKR’s argument that Zuraida’s RM10m bond was reasonable; decision reserved
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 14 — The Federal Court was told today that the High Court’s decision ordering former Ampang MP Datuk Zuraida Kamaruddin to pay RM10 million to Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) for breaching a bond with the party was reasonable.
PKR counsel Ranjit Singh submitted that there was an admission of fact that RM10 million, or a sum exceeding that amount, had been expended on Zuraida.
“Zuraida admitted that the value conferred upon her exceeded RM10 million, while the operative clause fixed RM10 million as the sum payable upon the occurrence of the stipulated events,” he said during PKR’s appeal against a Court of Appeal decision reducing the bond payment from RM10 million to RM100,000.
Ranjit submitted that the appeal ultimately turned on the legal consequence of a contractual admission of value where Section 75 of the Contracts Act is invoked.
“The recital recorded Zuraida’s admission that the value conferred upon her exceeded RM10 million. Section 75 remains the statutory control against penal, oppressive or unconscionable stipulations. But it must be applied to the contract as it stands, including the facts contractually admitted by the parties,” he said.
The counsel submitted that although the bond was contractual in nature, it had been executed against the backdrop of the country’s political landscape at the time, when political coalitions were prevalent, and party-hopping had become a scourge, amid concerns that it could lead to the collapse of governments.
“One must read the bond in a manner that explains why the sum of RM10 million was stipulated, which at first glance may appear excessive. But the reality is, look at what happened. The Sheraton Move led to the collapse of the Pakatan Harapan (PH) coalition at the Federal level,” he said. He was assisted by lawyer Navpreet Singh.
Meanwhile, Zuraida’s counsel Tan Sri Azhar Azizan Harun contended that there was no separate or special category of “political contract” that stood exempt from Section 75 of the Contracts Act.
“The party cannot use its status and position as a political party to bypass statutory protections against penalty clauses. Section 75 of the Act does not cease to apply merely because the contractual obligations arose in the context of a political party.
