“To hold otherwise would create, by judicial implication, an exception to Section 75. This court should not countenance such an approach,” said Azhar Azizan, who was assisted by counsel Nizamuddin Hamid.
Azhar said the relationship between a political party and its candidate was, in practical terms, institutional in nature. The individual candidate lacked equal legal bargaining power when negotiating the quantum of a unilateral bond imposed as the condition or price of candidacy.
“This unequal bargaining power is not dependent on the candidate’s seniority or position in the party. The bond demonstrates that it was not an individually negotiated agreement in which the respondent freely negotiated and agreed that RM10 million represented a reasonable measure of compensation in the event of default.
“It was imposed on the respondent by the party,” he said, adding that the RM100,000 imposed by the Court of Appeal was reasonable.
After hearing submissions from both parties, the three-member bench, chaired by Chief Justice Tun Wan Ahmad Farid Wan Salleh and comprising Chief Judge of Sabah and Sarawak Datuk Azizah Nawawi and Federal Court Judge Datuk Azmi Ariffin, reserved its decision for a date to be scheduled later.
On June 24, 2025, the Federal Court granted PKR leave to appeal the matter.
This followed the Court of Appeal’s decision on December 11, 2024, when a three-member panel upheld the High Court’s finding that Zuraida had breached the bond, but reduced the quantum payable from RM10 million to RM100,000.
The Court of Appeal’s ruling came after the High Court in Kuala Lumpur, on June 23, 2023, ruled in favour of PKR and ordered Zuraida to pay RM10 million in accordance with the bond’s terms. The presiding judge, Datuk Akhtar Tahir, held that the bond was a valid and binding contract.
The lawsuit had been initiated in 2020 by PKR secretary-general Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail on behalf of the party, claiming that Zuraida had violated the terms of a bond she signed before contesting in the 14th General Election in 2018.
Under the bond, Zuraida, a former Housing and Local Government Minister, was required to pay PKR RM10 million within seven days if she resigned from the party, joined another political party, or became an independent representative after being elected on the party’s ticket. — Bernama

Title: New Lawas Hospital expected to evolve into specialist centre to cut long‑distance referrals, says deputy health minister
Article:
LAWAS, Sept 14 — The new 76-bed Lawas Hospital is expected to evolve into a specialist hospital, thereby reducing the local population’s reliance on distant hospitals.
Deputy Health Minister Datuk Hanifah Hajar Taib stated that current manpower constraints have resulted in incomplete staffing at the hospital, a situation that will improve once additional personnel are secured.
“I hope that God willing, medical specialists will be permanently based at Lawas Hospital, rather than relying on scheduled visiting specialists.
“It has been difficult for the people to access specialist care, as they previously had to be sent to distant hospitals. I hope this facility will become a specialist hospital,” she said at the Lawas Hospital project handover ceremony here today.
The new hospital is equipped with, among other facilities, two operating theatres, a patient kitchen, an ICT lab enabling remote consultations with medical specialists, nine haemodialysis machines, and 76 beds, including four beds in the High Dependency Ward.
Hanifah noted that geographical factors make comprehensive health facilities in Lawas crucial; previously, patients requiring specialist referrals had to travel approximately one and a half hours to Limbang and about three and a half hours to Miri via certain routes.
Meanwhile, Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi, who also attended the ceremony, stated that the RM183 million Lawas Hospital project was built by the Public Works Department’s Special Project Team 2 starting June 30, 2020, using a Design and Build method undertaken by MCS Management Sdn Bhd.
He expressed hope that the hospital would improve community access to quality healthcare services and serve as a catalyst for enhancing the quality of healthcare service delivery in Lawas. — Bernama

Title: Abdul Aziz appointed Deputy Inspector‑General of Police
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 14 — Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) Management Director Datuk Seri Abdul Aziz Abdul Majid has been appointed Deputy Inspector-General of Police, effective September 9.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the appointment was consented to by His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, on the advice of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and upon the recommendation of the Police Force Commission, in accordance with Clauses 4 and 5 of Article 140 of the Federal Constitution.
“Abdul Aziz’s expertise and experience in policing, coupled with his strong leadership and competence, make him well suited to serve as Deputy Inspector-General of Police.
“The government congratulates him on his appointment,” he said in a statement today.
Abdul Aziz, 59, was born in Penaga, Penang, on February 19, 1967, and holds a Master of Social Sciences (Police Studies) from Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia (UKM).
He joined the PDRM on July 1, 1995, and has served in various departments throughout his career, including the Management Department, Special Branch, Criminal Investigation Department, Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department, Commercial Crime Investigation Department, Logistics and Technology Department, and Crime Prevention and Community Safety Department.
Abdul Aziz has held several key positions, including Management Director, Deputy Director of Special Branch, Deputy Director of Narcotics, Penang Police Deputy Chief, Principal Assistant Director of Management Policy/Human Resource, and Principal Assistant Director of the Special Integrated Investigation Team.
He has also attended various international courses and seminars, including the 8th International Symposium of Best Police Practice in Dubai, and the Intelligence Management Development Programme in Australia. — Bernama

Title: Sixteen drownings in Pahang this year, Bomba urges public to respect warning signs
Article:
KUANTAN, Sept 14 — A total of 16 drowning deaths have been recorded in Pahang so far this year, and the public is urged to prioritise safety when engaging in activities near rivers, waterfalls, and beaches.
Pahang Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) assistant director of operations and rescue, Mohd Salahuddin Isa, said key safety measures include heeding warning signs and refraining from swimming in areas identified as dangerous.
He added that visitors must also be vigilant regarding the “water surge” phenomenon particularly when at waterfalls, rapids, and rivers.
“To date, 16 drowning cases resulting in 16 deaths have been recorded across the state; we advise the public to always prioritise safety and understand the risks associated with recreational areas.
“Never swim in areas marked with red flags or ‘No Swimming’ warning signs,” he said in a statement today.
Mohd Salahuddin advised that if a person appears to be drowning, members of the public should not immediately jump into the water unless they possess rescue skills.
Instead, assistance can be provided using the ‘Reach, Throw, Row, Go’ concept: trying to reach the victim with a long object like a stick or pole (Reach), throwing a floating object such as a lifebuoy (Throw), using a boat if available (Row), or calling the 999 emergency line to dispatch the Water Rescue Team (PPDA) to the location (Go). — Bernama

Title: Court of Appeal slashes Muhammad Shafee’s damages in Malaysian Bar suit to RM120,000
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 14 — The Court of Appeal today reduced the damages awarded to senior lawyer Tan Sri Muhammad Shafee Abdullah from RM340,000 to RM120,000 in his suit against the Malaysian Bar and two others for breach of statutory duty.
A three-member bench led by Justice Datuk Dr Choo Kah Sing, and comprising Datin Paduka Evrol Mariette Peters and Datuk Meor Hashimi Abdul Hamid, unanimously allowed the Malaysian Bar’s appeal in part.
The bench also dismissed Muhammad Shafee’s appeal seeking an increase in the quantum of damages.
In delivering the decision, Justice Choo held that the damages and quantum sought must be established by facts, rather than mere inference.
He further held that although there were illegalities in the Bar’s action, it did not automatically follow that the action was taken with malice.
The Bar had appealed on the ground that the quantum of damages awarded by the High Court was excessive, while Muhammad Shafee cross-appealed, contending that the sum awarded was inadequate and challenging the High Court’s refusal to grant exemplary damages.
In April last year, the High Court awarded Muhammad Shafee RM200,000 for reputational loss and injury to feelings, RM100,000 for loss of professional opportunities, RM20,000 for mental stress and health-related consequences, and RM20,000 in aggravated damages. It did not award exemplary damages.
However, the Court of Appeal today reduced the award for reputational loss and injury to feelings from RM200,000 to RM100,000, while maintaining the RM20,000 in aggravated damages.
The appellate court set aside the awards for loss of professional opportunities, mental stress and health-related consequences.
In March 2015, Muhammad Shafee sued the Bar, former Attorney-General Tan Sri Tommy Thomas and former Court of Appeal Judge Tan Sri VC George, both of whom were practising lawyers at the time, as defendants.
Muhammad Shafee claimed that Thomas had published and submitted a motion on Feb 28, 2015, for discussion at the Malaysian Bar annual general meeting on March 14 the same year, and that the motion was seconded by George.
The motion concerned Muhammad Shafee’s involvement in a roadshow in a sodomy case in which he was the ad hoc prosecutor.
On May 26, 2016, the High Court dismissed Muhammad Shafee’s suit. He subsequently lost his appeal in the Court of Appeal on Oct 11, 2018, prompting him to bring the matter to the Federal Court.
On Oct 20, 2021, the Federal Court allowed Muhammad Shafee’s appeal, holding that he was entitled to damages from the Bar, and ordered the case to be remitted to the High Court for an assessment of damages.
The Bar then filed a review bid, which was dismissed by the Federal Court on Sept 19, 2022.
Following that assessment, on April 14 last year, the High Court awarded RM340,000 in damages to Muhammad Shafee.
At the Court of Appeal today, lawyers Lambert Rasa-Ratnam and Colin Yoong Shern Zian represented the Malaysian Bar, while Muhammad Shafee appeared on his own behalf together with lawyer Naresh Mayachandran. — Bernama

Title: Home minister confirms police investigating Negeri Sembilan MB Ismail Lasim’s duress claim
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 14 — Police have opened an investigation paper into Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim’s claim that he signed an instrument of proclamation with regard to the Yang di-Pertuan Besar against his will and under duress.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said further developments would be shared if there was progress in the investigation.
“The investigation paper has been opened and is still in progress. If there is any progress, as usual, we will share it with the media,” he told reporters after attending the Home Ministry’s monthly assembly here today.
Ismail was previously reported to have claimed that he was forced to sign the document before lodging a police report on September 8 to enable the authorities to conduct an investigation.
It was previously reported that Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the claim needed to be verified by the lawyers who were present during the signing process to establish whether it had occurred.
The Umno president also said the party would not interfere and would fully respect the royal institution, laws and customs in Negeri Sembilan. — Bernama

Title: Lim Guan Eng dares Zahid, demands Penang Pakatan expel Umno and defer hikes
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 14 — DAP’s Air Putih assemblyman Lim Guan Eng has questioned why Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi dared the Pakatan Harapan-led federal government to expel Umno from Putrajaya, but did not issue the same challenge to Penang’s PH administration.
Lim noted that Umno holds positions in the Penang state executive council, both city councils and state linked companies. He suggested Zahid lacked the courage to push Penang PH because the coalition would still retain a two thirds majority in the state assembly even without Umno’s two elected representatives.
He accused Umno of exploiting the Penang PH leadership’s hesitation over the party’s “duplicitous role” — working with opposition Perikatan Nasional while remaining part of the state government. Lim warned PH supporters were well aware that Umno and PAS would continue to pursue “extremist politics and divisive rhetoric” to win power at all costs.
Lim urged the Penang government to counter what he described as opportunistic and hypocritical behaviour by Umno and Barisan Nasional with people centric policies. He proposed deferring hikes in charges, quit rent, water tariffs and parking rates to close the door on Umno, PAS, MCA and Gerakan.

Title: Najib pardon delay not automatic, PAS claims objections triggered deferral
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 14 — PAS has called on the government to explain why the Federal Territories Pardons Board deferred consideration of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s application for a royal pardon.
The party argued the deferral could not have happened on its own, but only if instructions or objections were raised by members of the Pardons Board or other interested parties.
PAS secretary general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said the matter was of public interest and should not be withheld from the people.
“PAS demands that the government immediately clarify this issue to the public,” he added.
He stressed that transparency was essential in a case involving a former prime minister, and that the public deserved to know why Najib’s petition had been delayed.
Takiyuddin was referring to a statement issued by the Legal Affairs Division (BHEUU) of the Prime Minister’s Department on September 11, which confirmed that the 63rd meeting of the Pardons Board for Kuala Lumpur, Labuan and Putrajaya had been chaired by Sultan Ibrahim, the Yang di Pertuan Agong XVII.
The statement also noted His Majesty had consented to Najib’s petition being postponed to another meeting of the Pardons Board to be held at a later date.

Title: High Court acquits 15‑year‑old of Bandar Utama school murder, rules unsound mind
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Sept 14 — The High Court today acquitted and discharged a 15-year-old boy of the charge of murdering a female student at a secondary school in Bandar Utama, Petaling Jaya, last year.
Judge Adlin Abdul Majid then ordered the teenage boy to be placed at Hospital Bahagia Ulu Kinta, Perak, beginning today, for a period to be approved by the Sultan of Selangor.
Speaking to reporters outside the court, the teenager’s lawyer Kitson Foong said the court held that his client was of unsound mind at the time of the incident.
“The respondent (the teenage boy) was found to be of unsound mind at the hour, date and time of the incident in October (2025). Accordingly, the defence successfully raised Section 84 of the Penal Code. The court recorded an acquittal on the ground of insanity,” he said at a press conference after the proceedings.
He said the court’s findings established that there was medical insanity, which gave rise to a finding of legal insanity in respect of his client.
The teenager’s lawyer Kitson Foong said the court held that his client was of unsound mind at the time of the incident. — Bernama pic
Foong informed the media that the court also accepted the testimony of Consultant Forensic Psychiatrist at Hospital Bahagia Ulu Kinta, Dr Ian Lloyd Anthony, who confirmed that the teenager was suffering from severe and aggressive schizophrenia.
“The schizophrenia caused him to lose his sense of self. He believed he was a god. He said he heard voices and instructions from someone. The prosecution did not dispute this,” he said.
He said the teenager would begin receiving treatment for the disorder and noted that the recovery process would take time.
The lawyer said the judge had reminded the teenager to recognise that his actions had resulted in the loss of a life, and to be grateful for the second chance given to him.
Throughout the trial, the prosecution called 11 witnesses, while two defence witnesses, including the teenager himself, gave evidence.
The teenager was accused of murdering his schoolmate in a female student’s toilet at a national secondary school in Bandar Utama between 9.20am and 9.35am on Oct 14, 2025.
He was charged under Section 302 of the Penal Code, which provides for the death penalty, or imprisonment of between 30 and 40 years, and shall also be liable to not more than 12 strokes of the cane if not sentenced to death.
However, Section 97(1) of the Child Act 2001 stipulates that the death penalty shall not be imposed on a person under the age of 18.
In lieu thereof, the court may order the individual to be detained for a period approved by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, the Ruler or Yang di-Pertua Negeri, as provided under Section 97(2) of the same Act.
Deputy public prosecutors Raja Zaizul Faridah Raja Zaharudin, Aqharie Durranie Aziz and Ahmad Iqbal Azman appeared for the prosecution.
As the teenager is still a minor, his identity cannot be disclosed, and his photograph cannot be taken. The entire proceedings were conducted in closed court.
On Feb 12 last year, the teenager pleaded not guilty after the charge was read to him again in Mandarin before Judge Adlin. — Bernama

Title: Bintulu Port comes under Sarawak jurisdiction following repeal of federal Acts
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 14 — Bintulu Port has officially transitioned from a federal port to a state port under the jurisdiction of the Sarawak government, effective September 1, 2026.
Bintulu Port Holdings Bhd (BPHB) said in a filing with Bursa Malaysia that the transition follows the enactment of two acts — the Declaration of an Area in the Bintulu District to be a Federal Port (Repeal) Act 2024 [Act 858] and the Bintulu Port Authority (Dissolution) Act 2024 [Act 859].
It said Bintulu Port Sdn Bhd’s (BPSB) operation, management and development of Bintulu Port are governed by the heads of agreement dated July 27, 2026, entered into between the Sarawak government, Bintulu Port Authority (Sarawak) (BPA Sarawak) and BPSB, pending the execution of the Port Operation Concession Agreement (POCA).
“The Ministry of Infrastructure and Port Development, Sarawak, vide letter reference MIPD/700-12/1/1(47) on June 23, 2026, has notified BPSB, a wholly owned subsidiary of BPHB, that the government has approved in principle the appointment of BPSB as the approved port operator for Bintulu Port under Section 12(2)(a) of the Port Authorities Ordinance, 1961,” it said.
It added that the transition will not affect the day-to-day operations of Bintulu Port or the continuity of services to customers, port users and other stakeholders.
It said BPSB remains the operator of Bintulu Port and all port operations and services will continue without any interruption under the state regulatory framework.
“The board views the transition as a significant milestone for BPHB and BPSB.
“BPHB will continue to work closely with the state government of Sarawak, BPA Sarawak and all relevant authorities to support a smooth transition and maintain the stability, efficiency and continuity of port operations,” it said. — Bernama

Title: Fahmi warns that communalism and corruption can weaken Malaysia’s future
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 14 — Malaysia’s younger generation must understand the country’s history and appreciate the struggles of previous generations in building a peaceful and united nation, while rejecting corruption that could undermine the country’s future.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said there were three things that could destroy a country, namely communism, communalism and corruption.
He said communism had once posed a major threat to national security, with armed movements, killings and disruptions to public peace capable of undermining Malaysia’s stability.
“Although the threat of communism has been overcome, society must remain vigilant against anything that could undermine unity, including communalism... it can become a threat when someone puts their own race above others to the extent of looking down on or oppressing other races.
“As a leader, I now understand that holding a position is a trust. It is a responsibility and trust given to us to do good, and we must never betray that trust,” he said.
He said this when speaking at the JIWA@Komuniti National Day and Malaysia Day (HKHM) 2026 programme at Politeknik Kuching here today.
Fahmi said the formation of Malaysia was unique as it was achieved through consensus and negotiations, unlike some countries that had to go through conflict or armed struggles to achieve independence.
“Hence, the younger generation has an important role to play in ensuring that the history and values that shaped the country continue to be preserved so that Malaysia remains peaceful, united and progressive in the future,” he said. — Bernama

Title: KM263.6 southbound towards Menora Tunnel now safe for motorists after rapid slope‑erosion mitigation, says Perak exco
Article:
IPOH, Sept 14 — The state government has assured that the North-South Expressway (PLUS) route near KM263.6, southbound towards the Meru-Ipoh Utara (Menora) Tunnel, is now safe after the area experienced slope erosion on Sept 11.
Perak Infrastructure, Energy, Water and Transport Committee chairman Datuk Seri Mohammad Nizar Jamaluddin said that authorities have carried out immediate and continuous monitoring, along with mitigation measures, to ensure traffic safety at all times.
“Motorists are assured that travel along the route is safe, following prompt action by PLUS and the Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM), which covered the affected slope with waterproof sheeting and diverted rainwater. The route was reopened safely within less than 24 hours.
“The waterproof sheeting was installed to prevent rainwater from continuing to seep in and soften the soil structure in the event of subsequent rain,” he said during a visit to the site of the erosion, here today.
Yesterday, Perak police chief Alwi Zainal Abidin announced that the left lane at the landslide site would be closed to facilitate the installation of safety cones over a one-kilometre stretch from KM262.8 to KM263.8.
On long-term safety measures, Mohammad Nizar said PLUS is currently drafting proposals for slope structure reinforcement as well as the installation of steel netting in high-risk areas.
He said satellite monitoring in collaboration with the Public Works Department (JKR) may also be employed to detect rock or soil movement more quickly with greater accuracy, adding that this method was previously used during the landslide in Blue Valley (Pahang)
“We are also proposing the installation of 24-hour CCTV cameras at strategic locations and increased frequency of patrols by PLUS in high-risk areas,” he said.
He attributed the slope erosion to weather factors, noting that rainfall had been unusually high at 65 millimetres (mm), compared with the usual level of around 40 mm.
“So perhaps the resilience of the trees at that location was somewhat weak, causing them to fall and trigger the erosion,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Fire Dept working with Public Service Dept to ensure welfare of two officers missing in Nepal
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 14 — The Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) will ensure that the welfare of its two officers who remain uncontactable following flash floods in Rasuwa, Nepal last month is taken care of.
Its director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said the department had consulted the Public Service Department (PSD) on matters relating to the two officers’ salaries and pensions.
He said checks showed that JBPM headquarters deputy director of the Planning and Research Division Mohd Sani Harul is due to retire on September 23, while its Central Region Academy officer Mohd Fakhrul Munir Mohd Isa still has many years of service remaining.
“We will refer the matter to PSD regarding their welfare,” he told reporters at the Public Sector Human Resource Management Conference here today.
The two officers were among 10 Malaysians who departed for Nepal on Aug 24 to travel to Everest Base Camp (EBC).
The Foreign Ministry said today that 55 Malaysians remain uncontactable following the floods and landslides in Nepal and China, with efforts to establish the status of each individual still ongoing. — Bernama

Title: MAF ready to support emergency flying doctor service evacuations, says Chief of Defence Forces
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 14 — The Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) is ready to deploy its air assets to assist the Health Ministry (MoH) in providing Flying Doctor Service (FDS), particularly for emergency medical evacuations in remote areas.
Chief of Defence Forces Gen Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman said the move was aimed at meeting the ministry’s urgent needs following last Tuesday’s FDS helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Sarawak.
He said the MAF had sufficient facilities and helicopters to undertake the missions and was ready to cooperate once an official request was coordinated at ministry level.
“As a provider of services in the context of comprehensive security and emergency assistance, we will fill the gap during this critical period, particularly in areas that are difficult to access.
“We are ready to meet the ministry’s request and coordinate the operational efforts to ensure that services for the people are not disrupted,” he said during a special interview with the Chief of Defence Forces in conjunction with the 93rd MAF Day at Wisma Pertahanan here today.
Malek Razak, however, stressed that the MAF’s assistance would focus on emergency evacuation support and would not involve taking over the MoH’s routine medical operations in their entirety.
Yesterday, Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said four government agencies, including the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF), would assist the MoH in providing temporary mercy flights.
The alternative arrangement, which also involves the Royal Malaysia Police, Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency and Fire and Rescue Department, will remain in place pending the outcome of investigations and completion of safety improvements for FDS operations.
The BO-105 helicopter crash near the Long Lellang STOLport runway claimed five lives, including four MoH medical personnel.
The victims were pilot Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 30; medical officer Dr Ainul Baraah Kamarudin, 33; medical assistant Alexson Adit Henry, 31; and nurses Jessie Paya Jok, 44, and Debra Moset, 40. — Bernama

Title: MOF tours states to gather Budget 2027 input from industries, NGOs and public, says Amir Hamzah
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 14 — The Ministry of Finance (MOF) is conducting a budget tour to gather views and suggestions from industry players, non-governmental organisations (NGOs) and members of the public nationwide as it prepares for Budget 2027.
Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said the tour aims to gain insight into the needs of key sectors in each state and obtain input from parties directly affected by government policies and allocations.
“We are visiting every state to understand the industries that are important,” he told reporters after visiting Sekolah Menengah Agama Al-Mashoor (Girls) here today.
Amir Hamzah said Penang is among the locations due to its important role in the electrical and electronics (E&E) and semiconductor sectors.
The medical devices sector is also a focus of the Penang tour, given that Malaysia exports a wide range of medical equipment and is advanced in this industry, he said.
“This is one of the high-value economic sectors with the potential to boost domestic employment by creating better jobs here,” he said.
There will be a tour of Sabah and Perak before Penang to gather views from industry players, including those in the blue (maritime-based) economy and automotive sectors.
The government will study all views received through focus group sessions and meetings with stakeholders, he said, adding that some will be considered for inclusion in the budget.
The other proposals will be examined and discussed with the relevant ministries and agencies.
“The focus on specific groups has significantly contributed to enhancing the budget’s quality, given that we have looked beyond ministries and agencies to incorporate proposals from the industry, NGOs, and the public.
“This is to ensure that our budget is comprehensive and inclusive across all sectors,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Tabung Haji RCI chronology: Jamil Khir among five charged since report made public
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 14 — The disclosure of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report into the management and operations of Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) has triggered a series of investigations and legal proceedings, with a former minister becoming the latest person charged in court today.
Over the past several weeks, several individuals have been called in to give statements or detained to assist investigations, while five people have so far been charged at the Sessions Court here in connection with various cases.
In proceedings which began at 8.45am today, former Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Datuk Seri Jamil Khir Baharom pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court here to three charges involving RM860,308,770.51 in TH funds.
Apart from Jamil Khir, those charged were former TH chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim, former THP Bina Sdn Bhd Security and Safety Manager Nasahruddin Ahmad, and former TH Properties Sdn Bhd deputy general manager Tengku Kamarolhisham Tengku Kamaruddin, who was also a former deputy general manager of THP Bina Sdn Bhd.
Also charged was Alam Maritim Resources Bhd group managing director and group chief executive officer Datuk Azmi Ahmad.
Here is the chronology of the RCI on TH:
July 22, 2026:
Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Zulkifli Hasan says the proposal to make the final RCI report on TH public would be discussed at a Cabinet meeting.
July 23, 2026:
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim says the government was prepared to make the final RCI report on TH public in the near future to allow the public to know the findings of the investigation into allegations involving the sale of the agency’s strategic assets.
July 29, 2026:
The Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (JAKIM) publishes the RCI report on the investigation into TH’s management and operations from 2014 to 2020.
The Prime Minister stresses that anyone found responsible for losses suffered by TH based on the RCI findings would be brought to justice.
July 30, 2026:
The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) sets up a special team to review and scrutinise the RCI report on TH, which had been made public.
The Attorney General’s Chambers says it will immediately review the Commission’s findings.
Bernama July 31, 2026:
MACC begins its investigation, with eight officers deployed to the TH building.
August 5, 2026:
MACC records the statement of a former chief financial officer of a statutory body-owned company for more than six hours to assist investigations.
Police open five investigation papers after receiving nine reports from TH, its subsidiaries and members of the public concerning commercial crime cases, including matters raised in the TH RCI report.
August 7, 2026:
The Inland Revenue Board says it had begun investigations into the individuals identified.
August 11, 2026:
The Dewan Rakyat convenes to debate the TH RCI report.
August 12, 2026:
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil says the TH RCI report would be handed over to the authorities for a full investigation based on all findings and information contained in the report.
August 15, 2026:
MACC detains seven individuals comprising a chief executive officer (CEO), a company director, a former company director and four former TH senior management officers to assist investigations.
August 21, 2026:
The Royal Malaysia Police, through its Commercial Crime Investigation Department, open five investigation papers concerning cases involving TH.
A former TH CEO placed under remand for seven days to assist investigations into the misappropriation of investment and share funds worth about RM190 million following the disclosure of the RCI report.
August 26, 2026:
MACC detains a former TH chairman and former Secretary-General of the Treasury to assist investigations.
August 27, 2026:
The former TH chairman and former Secretary-General of the Treasury remanded for seven days.
September 1, 2026:
MACC detains a former minister.
September 2, 2026:
The former minister remanded for five days to assist investigations into issues involving the lease of a TH-related hotel in Saudi Arabia.
September 3, 2026:
Nasahruddin charged at the Sessions Court with three counts of criminal breach of trust involving RM72,000 in penalty collections related to a proposed office complex development project in Putrajaya. Tengku Kamarolhisham was charged with three counts of abetting Nasahruddin.
Meanwhile, a former TH chief operating officer was scheduled to be charged at the Shah Alam Sessions Court, but proceedings were postponed to September 24 as he was undergoing examinations and treatment for a heart condition.
September 6, 2026:
Remand of the former minister extended by two days.
September 8, 2026:
The former minister released on MACC bail.
September 9, 2026:
Abdul Azeez charged at the Sessions Court with using his position to secure the chairmanship of Putrajaya Perdana Berhad and persuading TH board members to approve a proposed RM193.5 million investment in the company.
Before being charged at the Sessions Court under the MACC Act, Abdul Azeez and two former senior TH officers were first brought before the court for remand proceedings, with Abdul Azeez detained for two days to assist investigations into an alleged cheating case involving TH hibah payments under Section 420 of the Penal Code.
September 9, 2026:
Police detain five individuals, including a former TH chairman and former CEO, to assist investigations into a case involving the institution.
September 10, 2026:
Azmi charged at the Sessions Court with two counts of cheating the Principal Officer of TH Alam Management Sdn Bhd over daily charter rates of supply vessels.
Abdul Azeez released after the police’s application to extend the remand of the former Baling MP to assist investigations under Section 420 of the Penal Code was rejected.
MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman says a former minister would be charged at the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court the following Monday in connection with the MACC investigation following findings in the TH RCI report.
He said three charges had been recommended against the individual under Section 403 of the Penal Code for dishonestly misappropriating property.
September 14, 2026:
Jamil Khir charged at the Sessions Court with three counts of causing TH to dispose of RM860,308,770.51, or SAR766,060,237 (Saudi Riyal), belonging to the institution to Saudi Arabia-based property development and project management company Al-Rawda Real Estate Development and Projects Management Co Ltd. — Bernama

Title: Negeri Sembilan Dewan Keadilan rules Sept 5 document treasonous, Tuanku Muhriz remains Yang di‑Pertuan Besar
Article:
SEREMBAN, Sept 14 — The Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU) has declared that six individuals who signed a document dated September 5 seeking to depose the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan acted in a manner considered treasonous under
adat
and law.
The Dewan said four of the signatories did not hold the positions they claimed, had issued unlawful directives to government officers, and attempted to remove Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir without the mandatory investigation required under the state constitution.
It ruled that no government officer should act on instructions based on the September 5 document, and directed the state administration to continue recognising Tuanku Muhriz as the Yang di-Pertuan Besar. The Dewan also instructed its secretary to lodge a police report against the six individuals, noting that four of them had signed the September 5, 2026 document without holding the offices they purported to represent.
The Dewan further expressed concern over a proposal to form a reconciliation committee under the state government, saying matters of adat fall solely under its jurisdiction as provided for in Article XVI of the Negeri Sembilan Constitution. It said it would seek clarification from the government on the committee’s terms of reference.
In its statement, the Dewan reaffirmed its July 31 decision that the proclamation dated April 19 was unconstitutional, as three of the four signatories were not recognised Undang at the time. It stressed that no investigation had ever been carried out, as required under Article X(1), and that Tuanku Muhriz had never been given notice or the opportunity to be heard.
The Dewan noted that the then menteri besar had refused to endorse the proclamation on April 20, rendering it void. It added that a subsequent attempt by a new menteri besar to sign the same proclamation did not revive it, as the function under Article X(2) had already been discharged.
It said announcements made on September 5 and September 8 had no effect, as they relied entirely on the flawed April 19 proclamation and a subsequent instrument dated August 3, which did not add legitimacy.
The Dewan emphasised that Tuanku Muhriz remains the lawful Yang di-Pertuan Besar and president of the Dewan, and that no vacancy exists. It also clarified the current holders of Undang positions: Datuk Klana Petra Muhammad Faris Johari (Sungei Ujong), Datuk Sedia Raja Haji Hassan Ab Hamid (Rembau), and Datuk Johan Pahlawan Lela Perkasa Setiawan Datuk Haji Muhammed Abdullah (Johol). The posts of Undang Luak Jelebu and Datuk Shahbandar Sungei Ujong remain vacant.
The Dewan concluded by urging all parties not to spread baseless claims about the institutions of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar and the Undang, stressing that these
adat
institutions are a trust held for the people and heirs, not the property of any party or individual.

Title: AI kiosk that can translate any language and file tourist reports? Saifuddin challenges staff to innovate
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 14 — Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution today challenged his staff to design a kiosk operated by artificial intelligence (AI) that can translate any language and file a report with the Malaysian authorities in Bahasa Melayu.
The senator described the kiosk machine as a “dream” that he wants to see materialised by his ministry as the Anwar government pushes for broad artificial intelligence adoption in day-to-day operations.
“We must embrace AI and thank God we started this three years ago,” he said at the ministry’s monthly assembly here.
“Now we are in the phase of realising this adoption and if one of the dreams I have is when tourists come here, doesn’t matter if in KLIA, Bukit Bintang, and then disaster struck — their bags were snatched, or they lose their passports, or they are assaulted.
“They may be Japanese, Arabs. How do they lodge a report? My dream is there will be this kiosk machine. The tourists can speak in their own language and the AI machine will translate it, and write the report for them instantly in Bahasa Melayu,” the minister added.
Malaysia has been aggressively positioning itself as a regional AI hub, leveraging strategic infrastructure investments, tax incentives and public-private partnerships to attract multinational tech giants.
Major global players, including Microsoft, Google and Nvidia, have recently committed billions of dollars toward developing hyperscale data centres, cloud regions and advanced AI infrastructure across the country.
Johor and the Greater Kuala Lumpur region, in particular, have emerged as primary focal points for digital infrastructure expansion in South-east Asia.
Government leaders said the public-sector drive toward AI integration aligns with the administration’s broader National Artificial Intelligence Roadmap 2021-2025 and the Madani Economy framework.
Under Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, the administration has urged civil servants to transition from conceptual AI strategies to practical, citizen-facing applications.

Title: Malaysia’s SMART team returns from Nepal humanitarian relief mission early this morning
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 14 — The Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (SMART), which participated in the Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) mission in Nepal, arrived safely in the country at 2am today.
SMART commander Senior Fire Superintendent I (PgKB 1) Abdul Manaf Che Isa said the team departed from Kathmandu at 3 pm yesterday (local time) aboard a Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) A400M aircraft, making a brief stopover in Kolkata, India, for refuelling.
“Upon arrival at RMAF Subang Air Base, we underwent health screenings conducted by Ministry of Health officials, and all 11 members involved in the mission were confirmed to be in good health,” he told Bernama here today.
Earlier, Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan had announced that the team was scheduled to return on Saturday or Sunday.
He stated that equipment belonging to the team, such as drones, had been handed over to rescue teams in Nepal for use in search operations for victims of flash floods and landslides in the country.
The SMART MAS01 team participating in the HADR mission arrived in the country via Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu, on Sept 5, bringing with them 12.4 tonnes of search and rescue (SAR) equipment. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia, Thailand strengthen energy ties with new joint development area agreements, says Akmal Nasrullah
Article:
BANGKOK, Sept 14 — Malaysia and Thailand today strengthened their energy partnership with the signing of a new Production Sharing Contract (PSC) and Gas Sales Agreement (GSA) for Block A-18-01 in the Malaysia-Thailand Joint Development Area (MTJDA).
Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir, who is on a two-day working visit to Thailand, said the agreements, signed in conjunction with Gastech 2026 here, would ensure continuity in the development of the block while reinforcing investor confidence and supporting the energy security of both countries.
Akmal said the move came at an important time as natural gas continued to play a major role in Malaysia’s energy system and socioeconomic growth, with the fuel projected to account for 56 per cent of the country’s total primary energy supply (TPES) by 2050.
“The priority is to ensure that energy resource development continues to attract investment and is supported by industry capabilities that can create sustained value.
“Certainty, continuity and confidence are essential to unlock investment, sustain production and secure long-term value,” he said in a statement on Monday.
The Block A-18-01 PSC was entered into by Malaysia-Thailand Joint Authority (MTJA), PC JDA Limited and PTTEP JDX, while the GSA also involves Petronas and PTT Public Company Limited.
Akmal said the progress achieved through Block A-18-01 provided a strong foundation for the continued development of the MTJDA, which represents nearly five decades of cooperation between Malaysia and Thailand.
He said the momentum from the latest agreements should pave the way for the next phase, involving the development of a new PSC and GSA for Block B-17-01.
“The momentum created today should pave the way for the next phase of developing a new PSC and GSA for Block B-17-01, as we continue to unlock the full potential of MTJDA for the benefit of both nations,” he said.
Akmal also said Malaysia looked to industry partners and contractors to bring the capital, technology, expertise and long-term commitment needed to develop the resource in a commercially viable and responsible manner.
Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul, Thai Energy Minister Akanat Promphan and Akmal witnessed the signing ceremony.
Meanwhile, Akanat described the MTJDA as a successful model of bilateral cooperation built on trust and shared interests, saying the new agreements marked another important phase in Malaysia-Thailand energy cooperation.
He said the initiative had the potential to stimulate investment, support sustainable development and contribute to shared prosperity. — Bernama

Title: No confidence motion? Negeri Sembilan Speaker says none filed against MB Ismail Lasim
Article:
SEREMBAN, Sept 14 — Speaker Datuk Seri Dr Awaludin Said today confirmed there is no motion of no confidence filed against Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim for the upcoming Negeri Sembilan state assembly sitting.
As reported by
The Star
, Awaludin said he has not received any official notice or heard of such a move following recent developments surrounding the
adat
issue in the state.
“I can deny that this will be brought up or tabled at the upcoming sitting. Also, I will only allow a motion if the state government has made a decision on it,” he was quoted as saying.
Awaludin was responding to speculation on social media that assemblymen from Barisan Nasional or Perikatan Nasional were planning to oust Ismail during the sitting scheduled for October 16.
The five-day sitting will be officially opened by the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.
According to
The Star
, Awaludin stressed that even if an emergency motion was tabled to remove Ismail, he would not allow it.
He said issues related to unverified matters could not be brought into the House, which he described as the highest legislative institution to make laws and policies.
He added that matters deemed illegal under state laws should first be resolved by the authorities, including the Dewan Keadilan dan Undang, before being raised in the assembly.
He appealed to the public to be patient and avoid speculation.
“For me, what is important is that the state government has been formed, the MB appointed, the exco and assemblymen sworn in.
“Let’s give the state government time to resolve the issues before us.
“Do not listen too much to allegations and assumptions which are mostly untrue,” he said.
On September 5, four individuals identifying themselves as the Undang Yang Empat, together with the Tunku Besar of Tampin and Dato’ Shahbandar of Sungei Ujong, alleged that Ismail had signed a proclamation endorsing the deposition of Tuanku Muhriz as state ruler. They claimed the document was signed at Istana Laguna Biru in Port Dickson on August 3.
Ismail later said he had signed the document under duress and lodged a police report. He also pledged loyalty to Tuanku Muhriz as the legitimate Yang di-Pertuan Besar.

Title: Federal govt allocates RM1.46b for eight flood mitigation projects in Melaka
Article:
MELAKA, Sept 14 — The federal government, through the Ministry of Energy Transition and Water Transformation (PETRA), has approved eight flood mitigation projects in Melaka worth a total of RM1.46 billion for the 2021–2026 period, aiming to enhance protection for residents in flood-prone areas.
Melaka Department of Irrigation and Drainage (JPS) director Mohd Adnan Ahmad Fauzi said these projects are part of the federal and state governments’ integrated efforts to reduce the risk and impact of flooding in the state.
He noted that the projects include the Alor Gajah Flood Mitigation Plan (RTB) Phase 1, Bandar Jasin RTB, Bandar Merlimau RTB, Sungai Putat RTB, and Sungai Duyong RTB, as well as the upgrading of the Krubong-Durian Tunggal Flood Mitigation Pond into a dual-purpose facility serving both flood mitigation and state water supply needs.
“Of the six projects currently underway, five are expected to be fully completed by the fourth quarter of 2027, while the remaining project is slated for completion in 2030.
“The two projects still in the pre-implementation stage are the Melaka River Flood Mitigation Project (RTB) Phase 1 and the Sungai Baru RTB in Alor Gajah; both are currently in the design phase,” he told Bernama.
Mohd Adnan said although none of the RTB projects have been fully completed to date, flood hotspot data released by the Melaka Department of Irrigation and Drainage (JPS) Hydrology Unit and the National Flood Forecasting and Warning Centre (PRABN) indicates a reduction in hotspots—from 157 in 2021 to 106 last year.
“Once all these RTB projects are fully completed, we anticipate that over 50,000 residents in Melaka will be protected against flood risks,” he said.
Mohd Adnan explained that the effectiveness of the ongoing projects is evaluated using flood monitoring data — covering frequency, duration, and depth of flooding, the extent of affected areas, and rainfall data.
He noted that this data is continuously monitored by the Melaka Water Resources and Hydrology Management Division and the PRABN to assist JPS in assessing the effectiveness of the implemented mitigation measures.
In a related development, Mohd Adnan mentioned that the flood mitigation approach in Melaka has shifted away from a sole focus on river widening; instead, it has moved towards integrated river basin management, spanning from upstream catchment areas down to the river mouth.
“The RTB project designs also take into account climate change patterns and the potential for more extreme rainfall events in the future, based on hydrological data, rainfall records, and climate change projections.
“However, flood mitigation projects cannot guarantee that flooding will be completely avoided, particularly during extreme rainfall events that exceed the design capacity of drainage and river systems,” he said.
He noted that improvements implemented in Melaka include the construction of more flood retention ponds, river upgrades, and the use of more efficient pump stations.
For instance, he cited the Sungai Baru Flood Mitigation Project (RTB) in Masjid Tanah, which proposes the creation of four flood retention ponds as a long-term measure to reduce recurring floods.
Mohd Adnan stated that the Department of Irrigation and Drainage (JPS) is also enhancing the use of digital technology and real-time data—including flood forecasting systems, online river level monitoring, automated rainfall data, and hydrological and hydraulic modeling—to enable early forecasting and faster response times.
He added that another flood mitigation project, with an estimated cost of RM145 million, has been submitted for the consideration and approval of the Ministry of Economy under the First Rolling Plan (RP1) of the 13th Malaysia Plan (RMK13).
“Flood management also requires cooperation from all parties; while JPS can build infrastructure, its effectiveness depends on development planning, developer discipline, and public awareness regarding the maintenance of drainage and river systems,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Haze: 11 areas record unhealthy API readings, with Sri Aman, Serian highest at 174 at 11am
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 14 — Eleven areas nationwide recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 11am today.
According to the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, three areas in Sarawak recorded unhealthy readings: Sri Aman and Serian (174) and Kuching (135).
Meanwhile, eight areas in Peninsular Malaysia also recorded unhealthy API readings, with the highest recorded at Johan Setia, Selangor (158), followed by Cheras in Kuala Lumpur (153), Nilai and Seremban (152 and 147), Pasir Gudang and Larkin, Johor (145 and 136), Putrajaya (134) and Alor Gajah, Melaka (115).
Overall, 55 areas recorded moderate API readings, while two areas recorded good readings.
An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, and 301 and above hazardous. — Bernama
